description:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff has requested that the County provide construction management services to facilitate the completion of improvements to the Sheriff’s Office located on 4700 W. Midway Road, Fort Pierce, Florida 34981. The facility is located on County-owned.
The Sheriff's Office was constructed in 1995 and has not been renovated or improved in over thirty (30) years. Most recently, the Evidence Division has moved out of the Sheriff's Office and moved to the new Sheriff's Evidence Building recently constructed and opened on Rock Road.
Therefore, it is the Sheriff's desire to renovate and make efficient use of this available space and provide any other identified necessary improvements using approved FY'26 Maintenance Improvement Project Funding (FMIP) in the amount of $200,000.00 as well as Funds received from insurance towards the damages caused by a tornado during Hurricane Milton to the Sheriff's Office property in the amount of $727,651.17. The County will retain the FMIP $200,000.00 to pay for architect fees and the Sheriff's Office will receive an amount not to exceed $727,651.17 to pay for all construction expenses related to this renovation project.
Under the terms of the Interlocal Agreement, the County’s responsibilities are as follows:
Provide construction management services for the Project.
Schedule and conduct regular meetings with the contractor selected by the Sheriff.
Monitor progress of the construction of the Project and provide written reports to the Project Manager for the Sheriff.
Provide required design and permitting work for this project through the county approved architect not to exceed $200,000.00.
Provide up to an additional $727,651.17 in funding for construction of this project.
Under the terms of the Interlocal Agreement, the Sheriff’s responsibilities are as follows:
Contract with a licensed and insured contractor to construct the Project.
Require the Contractor to provide a public construction bond, builder’s risk insurance and obtain required building permits.
Require the Contractor to add the County as an additional named insured on the Contractor’s general liability and workers’ compensation policies.

description:
The Planning & Development Services Department — Building Division — is requesting to utilize funds from the Building Enterprise Fund to electronically scan historic building permit files that are currently stored at the County's Logistics facility.
The Department began scanning historical documents in FY20, with one staff member hired through the Manpower staff agency working continuously on this project.
In order to efficiently complete this project and improve public transparency and customer service, PDS is requesting the use of existing funds within the Building Fund to add 3 additional Manpower employees to assist. The Department has made arrangements with the Facilities Department to locate the additional Manpower staff at logistics, to improve efficiency. There are currently +/-33,388 files, including large plan sets, that need to be scanned and indexed. It has been estimated that this project, with four staff members, will take four years to complete.
Electronic file retention is essential to preserving historical permit records, reducing reliance on physical storage, and improving the County’s ability to respond efficiently to public records requests, property research inquiries, permitting reviews, and compliance activities. Establishing and maintaining digital access to historical permit records strengthens operational efficiency, transparency, and long-term records management.
The estimated cost of this project is approximately $250,000 annually. Therefore, the total cost for this project is estimated to be approximately $1,000,000.

description:
On November 12, 2020, the St. Lucie County Board of County Commissioners held a public hearing, duly noticed the St. Lucie News Tribune, to accept the 2020 Port of Fort Pierce Master Plan completed by Moffat & Nichol/Atkins on November 4, 2020. Subsequently, the Board approved Resolution 2020-255 on the same day, confirming a new direction for the Port of Fort Pierce that was consistent with the County’s Comprehensive plan.
A critical element of the 2020 Port of Fort Pierce Master Plan was/is the future development of the County-owned Harbour Pointe Park. This parcel is situated at the northern end of the Port Planning Area and sits adjacent to Taylor Creek. This area was identified in the plan as a mix of both recreational and marine commercial uses. A critical component of the plan required land acquisition/exchange, and a reconfiguration of Avenue M Ext., which was sited within private property. Through exchange agreements with the City of Fort Pierce and Destin Beach Inc. (DBI, Inc. - the adjacent port property landowner) the County acquired new lands contiguous to the historic park, some of which are positioned to establish a formal connection between North 2nd Street and the expanded Harbour Pointe Park.
Work Authorization No. 01 (Inwood Consulting Engineers) was previously approved by the Board for the design and permitting of a new entrance road to the park. Per the DBI, Inc. exchange agreement with the county, the unimproved “old” Avenue M Ext. roadway (including drainage) previously used for park access closed 18 months post-closing (March 26, 2026) and will be fully decommissioned soon.
Bidding of the new entrance road is imminent and the attached proposal from JMT is proposed for CEI & Geotechnical Services.

description:
The Environmental Resources Department (ERD) is working toward the goal of acquiring lots within a 486-acre subdivided area northwest of Turnpike Feeder Road that contains approximately 215 lots total. The area is identified in the 2004 SLC Native Habitat Inventory as an “A” based on high-quality native habitat coverage and potential for rare or endemic species. Approximately 115 lots have already been acquired. County staff has been monitoring the area to determine if any properties are available. On May 4, 2026, a parcel was offered for bid in a Tax Deed Auction. On the day of the auction, the tax deed was rescheduled to June 22, 2026. This parcel is located adjacent to Turnpike Feeder Road and southwest of US Highway 1. In recent appraisals of the adjacent land-locked parcels, a value of $7,500.00 was identified. Tax Deed 25-452 - Parcel I.D. No. 1406-333-0016-000-7 - .49 acres - Starting Bid - $1,860.78
As part of the Tax Deed Application process, the Clerk's Office orders a Property Information Report. Upon review of the reports dated January 26, 2026, there do not appear to be any title defects that may affect County ownership. A search of the Clerk's Official Records did not reveal any liens or judgments. The County has performed Phase I Environmental Assessments on several recent acquisitions north and south of the subject parcel.
By acquiring this parcel through a Tax Deed Auction, staff can reduce the cost to taxpayers by eliminating the need for an appraisal, title commitment and associated closing costs, and environmental assessments. The County must submit a maximum bid for each tax deed auction. The tax deed software automatically bids the auction at $100.00 increments until the highest maximum bid is reached, and gives the opportunity for last minute bidders to submit a counter-bid should they have sufficient deposit funds. If there is no counter-bidder, the County would be declared the auction winner at the starting bid.
Discussion
In the event the Board determines to authorize the County to bid at the public tax deed auction on the Turnpike Feeder parcel, County staff has determined that the County will need to take the following statutory steps:The County must register before the public sale
The County must deposit 5% of the County's highest bid with the Clerk prior to the public sale (the County currently has leftover funds in the deposit account from May 4 auction date)
If the County is the successful (i.e. highest) bidder, the County must deposit the balance of the purchase proceeds by 2:00 p.m. on the day after the public sale (in this case by June 23, 2026 at 2:00 p.m.)

description:
The Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) is proposing a project to improve the US-1 corridor in St. Lucie County. The project objective is to improve chronic flooding issues along SR-5/US-1 between Edwards Road and Tennessee Avenue, and along Virginia Avenue from Oleander Boulevard to US-1, both major hurricane evacuation routes within the City of Fort Pierce in St. Lucie County. The permanent solution will provide a constructible, cost-effective, and quality product to roadway, canal and pond end users that meets regulatory agencies' requirements of avoidance and minimization of impacts to the natural environment and existing roadway/utilities/canal/pond configuration and right-of-ways. The primary strategies involved may include:
• Replace and supplement existing drainage system along US-1 to control spread and meet
hydraulic grade line (HGL) criteria for the design storm events.
• Shoulder rocking and addition of curb and gutter or drop curb.
• Dredging and replacing side drains along the Savannah Road Outfall Ditch.
• Constructing french drain in the median to treat and provide runoff attenuation.
• Construction of sidewalk gaps, milling, resurfacing and overbuild to correct cross slope
deficiencies, lighting, signalization, and pavement marking upgrades.
FDOT has requested the County execute the attached License for Parcel 900.1 owned by St. Lucie County adjacent to US-1. The License will allow for restoration of the sidewalk, curb and gutter, and driveway(s) that are beyond the existing right-of-way line and for sloping, grading, tying in, harmonizing and reconnecting features with the US-1 improvements.

attachments.name: Chapter 18- Emergency Management Ordinance Revision - v5-Clean

description:
The Public Safety Department has completed a comprehensive revision of the County's Emergency Management Ordinance under Chapter 18 to modernize the framework governing emergency management and ensure full compliance with Section 252.38, Florida Statutes. This effort reflects a proactive approach that seeks to safeguard the health, safety, and welfare of residents through several key updates:Organizational Realignment: Formally establishes the Emergency Management Division within the Public Safety Department and designates the Public Safety Director as the Emergency Management Director.
Emergency Powers and Transparency: Updates the criteria for declaring a Local State of Emergency, limiting declarations to seven-day increments and mandating that all emergency orders be filed with the Clerk and posted on a dedicated public webpage.
Systemic Resilience: Mandates that all County departments maintain Continuity of Operations Plans (COOP) and internal chains of succession to ensure the continuation of essential services during disasters.
Health Care Industry Standards: Creates a new Article V to establish uniform procedures for the review and certification of disaster preparedness plans for healthcare facilities regulated by AHCA, DCF, and APD.
Public Accountability: Requires the presentation of After-Action Reports (AARs) to the Board within 90 days of an exercise or major activation to identify and track corrective actions.

attachments.name: 5-14-26 Recycling Processing ILA between IRC and SLC

description:
On November 19, 2019, St. Lucie County entered into an Interlocal agreement with Indian River County Solid Waste Disposal District ("Indian River") that allowed Indian River to deliver its recyclable materials to St. Lucie's recycling facility.
On November 15, 2020, St. Lucie County amended that Interlocal agreement with Indian River County Solid Waste Disposal District ("Indian River") allowing Indian River to provide St. Lucie's facility with recyclable materials that Republic Services will collect in the City of Palm Bay, Florida and transport to Indian River's Recycling Transfer Facility. In 2023, collection in the City of Palm Bay, Florida and transport to Indian River's Recycling Transfer Facility ceased.
St. Lucie notified Indian River that St. Lucie did not intend to renew the Interlocal Agreement when it expired on September 30, 2025; and St. Lucie and Indian River now wish to revise and clarify their respective obligations, which they intend to accomplish by replacing the existing Interlocal Agreement with this Agreement.
Proposed Interlocal AgreementAn outline of the business terms negotiated by Public Utilities and Administration follows:
Indian River agrees to deliver its Municipally Collected Solid Waste and Recyclable Materials to the County's System.
The County agrees to accept and manage the Solid Waste and Recyclable Materials that Indian River delivers.
The County will accept only those Recyclable Materials that are identified in Exhibit "A" to the Interlocal Agreement.
The County will charge and Indian River will pay the following rates (Per Ton Fee) for the County's services:
Table 1: Per Ton Fee schedule:
Recycling (per ton)
Non-conforming Material (per ton)
October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2030
$45
$79
The County and Indian River will share the net proceeds (profits) from the County's recycling program. The County shall receive one-half (50%) of the net revenue. Indian River shall receive part or all of the remaining one-half (50%) of the net revenue, subject to the provisions in Exhibt C (Section 5) of the Interlocal agreement. The Indian River's share of the net revenue shall be prorated, based on the percentage of the total tonnage of Program Materials and segregated cardboard (Old Corrugated Cardboard or "OCC") delivered by Indian River in relation to the total tonnage of such materials received by the County from all sources during the applicable Fiscal Year. The formula for calculating Indian River's share shall be as follows:
Indian River Share = (Indian River Tons ÷ Total Tons) x 50% x Net Revenue
For example, if during a given Fiscal Year, Indian River delivers 6,000 tons of Program Materials and segregated OCC to the County, and the total combined tonnage from all sources is 10,000 tons, then the Indian River 's portion would be 60% of the total tonnage. If the net revenue for that Fiscal Year is $200,000, the Indian River 's share of the net revenue would be: (6,000 ÷ 10,000) x 50% x $200,000 = $60,000.
The term of the Interlocal Agreement shall start on October 1, 2026, and end on September 30, 2030. At the end of the initial term, this Agreement shall be renewed and extended automatically for an additional one (1) year terms, with the final expiration of the Agreement being September 30, 2032.
meeting: Board of County Commissioners Regular Meeting
title: Interlocal Agreement (ILA) for Recycling Services between St. Lucie County and Indian River County

description:
For many years, St. Lucie County Utility District (SLCU) has worked to bring central sewer service to North Hutchinson Island (NHI). With this construction project, SLCU proposed to replace the existing septic tanks with central sewer service in the following subdivisions: Coral Cove, Fort Pierce Shores, and Jackson Way.
The request for bids, St. Lucie County Bid No. 24-066, for the Construction Contract of the North Hutchinson Island Septic to Sewer Project was advertised on May 12, 2024. A mandatory pre-bid meeting was held on May 30, 2024, and bids were opened on July 17, 2024. The bids were reviewed by consulting engineers CDM Smith Inc. for their recommendation.
Three (3) qualified contractors submitted bids, which varied from a low of $11,819,585.00 to a high of $25,007,715.95. The lowest bidder was CK Contractors and Development, LLC of West Plam Beach, Florida. CDM Smith, Inc. reviewed all three (3) submitted bids, verifying qualifications and references.
Board approved contract C24-09-783 on September 3, 2024 with CK Contractors and Development, LLC in the amount of $11,819,585.00.
Change order #1 was approved by Administration on April 10, 2026 which added 120 days to the contract term.
Attached is a copy of Change Order #2 adding additional restoration along the pipeline path to the Coral Cove and Fort Pierce Shores project areas at a cost of $407,582.83. This will provide for a more finished project area.

description:
River Park is an existing neighborhood off Prima Vista Boulevard which encompasses approximately 150 acres of single-family residential homes. River Park was developed prior to modern stormwater regulations and is not served by municipal wastewater utilities. River Park relies on vegetated roadside swales, which provide limited water quality treatment. Eight baffle boxes were designed and constructed to improve water quality along the north fork of the St. Lucie River. The installation of these baffle boxes has significantly enhanced stormwater treatment within the surrounding watershed, resulting in measurable water quality improvements to the St. Lucie River system. The following construction budget is the sum of three different contractors awarded contracts to construct the project.Construction budget:
Base Cost: $1,491,653.07
5% Contingency: $ 74,582.65
Total Construction Budget: $1,566,235.72
The total amount spent on the construction was $1,542,749.40, which includes all contingencies for unforeseen or unanticipated work approved by staff. The project was completed under budget with a remaining amount of $23,486.32.
Staff monitored the construction and determined the project was completed in substantial conformance with plans and specifications.

description:
The County has contracted with Timothy Rose Contracting to resurface the asphalt on Glades Cut Off Road from Midway Road to Selvitz Road during Fiscal Year 25/26. The work is expected to take two months to complete. The noise and vibration from the work may or may not violate the County Noise Control Ordinance, Chapter 28, Article V, which exempts noise resulting from construction activities only between the hours of 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM on weekdays.
The Average Annual Daily Traffic (AADT) reported in the St. Lucie County Transportation Organization's "Traffic Counts and Level of Service Report 2025" was 10,534 vehicles per day from Midway Road to Jenkins Road and 6,441 vehicles per day from Jenkins Road to Selvitz Road. The closest residences to the work area are located approximately 0.25 miles from Glades Cut Off Road. In accordance with Section 28-112 of the St. Lucie County Code of Ordinances, Timothy Rose Contracting is requesting a special permit to perform milling and repaving between the hours of 7:00 PM to 5:00 AM, Sunday through Friday night for safety purposes and to avoid traffic impacts and delays to the traveling public. The permit can be revoked with 24 hours’ notice to the contractor, if deemed necessary by the County.

description:
Sunland Gardens is a 415-acre residential community located in the northwestern part of St. Lucie County. The community was built before stormwater regulations existed and lacks modern drainage and water quality improvements. In 2024, utilizing Federal American Rescue Plan (ARP) dollars, a stormwater master plan was completed for Sunland Gardens. This master plan will serve as a baseline for future drainage improvements in the community.
This request is to fund engineering, design and permit efforts for Phase 1 stormwater improvements to the Sunland Gardens community. This first phase will address the north-west section of the community, located south of the Belcher Canal, east of Angle Rd., and west of N 41st St. Three (3) draft drainage improvement plans will be submitted to the County for review and will include updated drainage infrastructure, water quality improvements (baffle boxes), and updated roadways. Johnson, Mirmiran & Thompson Consulting Engineers (JMT) have submitted a proposal in the amount of $249,933.00. Design and permitting for Phase 1 should take approximately 18 months to complete. Future funding for Phase 1 construction would need to be identified upon completion of this effort.

description:
This is a request to amend the Future Land Use Map category for a +/-42 acre site, located on the east side of Old FFA Road one-half of a mile south of Angle Road, from RS (Residential, Suburban) which permits a maximum of 2 dwelling units per acre to MXD (Mixed-Use Development) with specific use area policies that limit development to residential at a maximum density of 2.95* dwelling units per acre. The specific use activity area policies assign land toward a future K-8 public school and require preservation of no less than ten acres of native upland habitat. The subject land area is proximate to the Serenoa PUD, which was approved by the BOCC for 319 dwelling units (density of 2.8 DU/A) and adjacent to the proposed Sunnyland Farms PUD which proposes 458 units on +/-230 acres for a density of 1.99 DU/A.
Because the subject land area is less than fifty (50) acres, state law designates it a Small-Scale Amendment. As such, there is no transmittal public hearing before the Board, only the adoption public hearing.
*Since the original hearing date, the applicant has reduced the proposed MXD density from 3.09 dwelling units per acre to 2.95, which equates to a six (6) unit reduction.
At the Applicant’s request, the Board continued the April 7th public hearing until April 21, 2026. On April 21, 2026, the Board again opened the public hearing and, at the Applicant’s request, continued it until May 19, 2026. Subsequently, the Applicant proposed a change in the sub-area policies for this MXD Future Land Use category. Previously, the specific use area policies capped residential density at 3.09 DU/A. Now a maximum residential density of 2.95 DU/A is proposed. Reducing the maximum density from 3.09 DU/A to 2.95 DU/A on the subject +/-42.01 acres will reduce the maximum unit count from 130 to 124.

description:

The proposal includes the dedication of nearly 7 acres for a future K-8 public school and provides nearly 45% of total site area as common open space, including ten acres of preserved native upland habitat. Common open space of +/-18.9 acres is more than one-half of the site area, after dedication of the school site.
This request for approval of the rezoning and Preliminary Development Plan, as proposed, can only be granted if the Board also determines to approve the companion request to amend the Future Land Use Map from RS (Residential Suburban) to MXD (Mixed Use Development) with specific use activity area policies limiting development to residential and capping density at no more than 2.95* DU/A.
*Since the original hearing date, the applicant has reduced the proposed density from 3.09 dwelling units per acre to 2.95 dwelling units per acre, which equates to a six (6) unit reduction.
At the Applicant’s request, the Board continued the April 7th public hearing until April 21, 2026. On April 21, 2026, the Board again opened the public hearing and, at the Applicant’s request, continued it until May 19, 2026. Subsequently, the Applicant proposed a change to the PUD maximum density by removing one 6-unit building. Previously, the residential density was at 3.09 DU/A. Now a maximum residential density of 2.95 DU/A is proposed. Reducing the maximum density from 3.09 DU/A to 2.95 DU/A on the subject +/-42.01 acres will reduce the maximum unit count from 130 to 124.

attachments.name: Proposed Interlocal Agreement by and between SLC and SLCSO for K9 Training Facility

description:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff (“Sheriff”) has requested that the County provide construction management services to facilitate the completion of improvements to the Sheriff’s K9 Training Facility located at 8805 Colbourn Road, Fort Pierce, Florida 34945. The facility is located on County-owned property commonly referenced as the Colbourn Property.
The current phase of the project consists of the construction of a covered pavilion to support training and operational activities for the Sheriff’s Office K9 Unit. The pavilion project is intended to enhance training capability, operational readiness, safety, and working conditions for handlers and canines. The proposed work generally includes construction of an approximately 621-square-foot roofed pavilion, slab and structural components, training-specific features (scent wall, chevron wall, and storage), related site work, and associated utility coordination.
The K9 facility has also benefited from significant private donor support. Mr. William Theroux and his late wife, Maureen, were instrumental in the conceptual design and funding of the existing K9 Training Facility, and Mr. Theroux has remained engaged in the continued improvement of the site, including the pavilion concept.
Florida law allows local government units to cooperate by agreement to provide necessary and essential public services. In that regard, attached is an Interlocal Agreement, which, if approved, would allow the County and the Sheriff to work together on the K9 Training Facility pavilion improvements similar to how the parties completed the Sheriff’s Property and Evidence Building.
Under the terms of the Interlocal Agreement, the County’s responsibilities are as follows:
Provide construction management services for the Project.
Schedule and conduct regular meetings with the contractor selected by the Sheriff.
Monitor progress of the construction of the Project and provide written reports to the Project Manager for the Sheriff.
Under the terms of the Interlocal Agreement, the Sheriff’s responsibilities are as follows:
Contract with a licensed and insured contractor to construct the Project.
Require the Contractor to provide a public construction bond, builder’s risk insurance and obtain required building permits.
Require the Contractor to add the County as an additional named insured on the Contractor’s general liability and workers’ compensation policies.

description:
Library Services is requesting approval of a revision to the Patron Code of Conduct Policy to establish age requirements for unattended minors.
The current policy, recently amended and approved by the Library Advisory Board on May 14, 2026, and last amended and approved by the St. Lucie Board of County Commissioners on July 16, 2019, does not define age guidelines for minors using the library without supervision, resulting in inconsistent practices and situations involving young children left unattended.
The proposed revision clarifies that children under the age of 12 (twelve) may not be left unattended in library facilities. Children/Youth ages 12 to 17 (twelve to seventeen) may use the library independently.
These updates provide clear expectations for caregivers, support consistent staff response, and enhance the safety and well-being of minors while maintaining the library’s commitment to public access and is in alignment with (PT1.4.1 Deliver Consistent Services — Review and improve policies/procedures to ensure quality service delivery for all end users.)

On July 24, 2018, the Board of County Commissioners approved Resolution No. 18-132, committing to provide economic incentives for a new manufacturing facility owned by Accel International Holdings, Inc. Subsequently, on May 18, 2021, the Board approved JGIG Agreement No. 21-003 for the creation of 125 full-time equivalent jobs in St. Lucie County paying more than 107% of the average county wage.
JGIG Agreement No. 21-003 has been amended four times due to project delays and changes to the job creation schedule. Most recently, on January 21, 2025, the Board approved the Fourth Amendment to JGIG Agreement No. 21-003, reducing the Year One job creation commitment from 63 jobs to 18 jobs.
Accel met its Year One job creation goal by creating 18 jobs in 2025.
On February 17, 2026, Accel submitted a letter requesting a two-year pause on its incentives and an extension of its job creation milestones. At the March 10, 2026, Board of County Commissioners Informal Meeting, staff presented the request, and the Board directed staff to terminate the existing agreement and renegotiate a new agreement that accounts for any changes to the County’s economic incentive program criteria.
On April 24, 2026, Accel submitted a letter supporting termination of the existing JGIG Agreement.
Revocation of Resolution No. 18-132 and termination of JGIG Agreement No. 21-003 will not affect Accel’s ability to request future economic incentives from the Board of County Commissioners.

description:
The Board of County Commissioners previously approved a contract with ROK Technologies to migrate and host the County's Geographic Information Systems (GIS) data in a Cloud-based environment on 5/21/2024.
An addition to the ROK Technologies Master Service Agreement has been provided to the County, making this the first amendment to the contract. This first amendment supplements the County's contracted server storage space. This increases the amount of storage that ROK allocates for the County's hosted feature services that support web maps and field collection applications as well as storage used for cloud-based storage of files, imagery, and web assets.
As the County continues to leverage Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for critical data analysis and decision-making processes, the need for reliable and secure hosting solutions for our ArcGIS Enterprise environment has become increasingly apparent. The availability of our GIS systems and services is essential to several integrated systems, including EnerGov (Online Permitting/Land Use Management), Public Works Department's Work Order/Asset Management system, and OneSolution OSSI (Computer Aided Dispatch). To maintain and enhance the efficiency, security, and scalability of our GIS infrastructure, the GIS Division has previously contracted with ROK Technologies to manage the hosting of our ArcGIS Enterprise environment.
This contract with ROK provides several benefits, including:
Enhanced Security and Compliance
Improved Reliability and Uptime (GIS services will be available should our network be compromised or be offline for any reason)
Comprehensive 24/7 Support
Scalability and Flexibility
In addition, there are avoided costs, including the cost of replacing servers/hardware and professional services or additional staff for ArcGIS Enterprise administration. Many organizations employ a full-time ArcGIS Administrator; this role is currently being filled by existing staff to the detriment of other projects. The time spent on ArcGIS Enterprise and database administration is easily equal to 1 FTE.

description:
The Public Safety Communications Division is responsible for maintaining accurate, validated, and continuously updated GIS and addressing data that directly supports E911 and NG911 call routing, location validation, and emergency response. These functions are foundational to 911 operations and are governed by NG911 standards, vendor specifications, and State of Florida E911 requirements.
Historically, these responsibilities were assigned to a dedicated GIS Coordinator role within the Public Safety Communications Division. The official job description for that position establishes that the role was responsible for the design, implementation, operation, and ongoing maintenance of NG911 GIS programs, including MSAG databases, ALI reconciliation, emergency service boundaries, and the provision of required NG911 datasets to external vendors and core services platforms.
While the position is no longer filled, the functions and responsibilities remain mandatory and must continue to be performed to ensure uninterrupted and compliant NG911 operations.
GEOComm is uniquely qualified to perform these services due to its:Demonstrated expertise in NG911 GIS data standards, validation, and maintenance
Proven experience managing MSAG and ALI reconciliation workflows
Direct familiarity with NG911 core services environments and Motorola Web DMS provisioning requirements
Ability to perform both the required true-up and ongoing maintenance under a coordinated, auditable service model
Public Safety is able to piggyback the General Service Administration (GSA) Contract Number GS-35F-0594S. Engaging GEOComm ensures continuity of required NG911 GIS functions that were previously assigned to an internal role, while providing a sustainable and compliant long-term solution.
Failure to ensure these functions are performed presents significant operational and public safety risks, including:Increased likelihood of misrouted 911 calls due to inaccurate or unsynchronized data
Delayed emergency response caused by incorrect caller location information
Inability to meet NG911 vendor and regulatory requirements
Increased liability exposure related to data integrity failures
Unsustainable reliance on ad-hoc processes that do not provide continuous validation or accountability

description:
Staff is undertaking a project to improve the water quality from a residential community between Sherwood Lane and Nicholas Road near Edwards Road. The Edwards Road Baffle Box proposes infrastructure east of S. 25th Street, between Sherwood Lane and Nicholas Road to the north of Edwards Road. The neighborhood flows into a drainage swale along a 25-foot drainage easement to the rear of the homes on Sherwood Lane. The drainage swale carries stormwater runoff south towards Edwards Road, into a North St. Lucie River Water District Canal, and ultimately discharging into Five-mile Creek. The area has limited drainage capacity due to the age of the community (est. 1960s) and the project area is within the Five Mile Creek/Ten Mile Creek North priority basin, as identified in the County's recent Stormwater Master Plan update. The location is also within the limits of the St. Lucie River BMAP and the project, once constructed, could assist the County towards the State-mandated nutrient reductions for the St. Lucie River.
The proposed project will improve water quality by constructing a 2nd generation baffle box along with related drainage improvements. This request will fund engineering design and study to review existing conditions and propose potential solutions for the area drainage. WRMA, Inc. submitted a formal proposal to complete the design in the amount of $149,825.00. Staff have reviewed the proposal and are recommending approval for the project.

JGIG Agreement No. 21-003 has been amended four times due to project delays and changes to the job creation schedule. Most recently, on January 21, 2025, the Board approved the Fourth Amendment to JGIG Agreement No. 21-003, reducing the Year One job creation commitment from 63 jobs to 18 jobs.
On June 4, 2024, the Board of County Commissioners approved an ad valorem tax exemption for Accel via Ordinance No. 2024-23, for a period of 10 years.
Accel met its Year One job creation goal by creating 18 jobs in 2025 and received an ad valorem tax exception in accordance with Ordinance No. 2024-23.
On February 17, 2026, Accel submitted a letter requesting a two-year pause on its incentives and an extension of its job creation milestones.
At the March 10, 2026, Board of County Commissioners Informal Meeting, staff presented the request, and the Board directed staff to terminate the existing agreement and renegotiate a new agreement that accounts for any changes to the County’s economic incentive program criteria.
On April 24, 2026, Accel submitted a letter supporting termination of their existing JGIG Agreement and ad valorem tax exemption.
Revocation of Ordinance No. 2026-15 will not affect Accel’s ability to request future economic incentives from the Board of County Commissioners.

description:
The Board of County Commissioners previously established the Economic Development Impact Fee Mitigation Program to encourage job creation, capital investment, and the expansion or relocation of qualified target industry businesses within St. Lucie County. The existing program has relied on fixed eligibility thresholds and mitigation formulas that do not fully reflect the County’s current economic development priorities or allow for consistent evaluation of overall project impact.
The proposed ordinance modernizes the program by establishing a scoring-based framework that evaluates projects based on measurable public benefits, including wage levels, job creation, capital investment, and catalytic economic impact. The revised structure is intended to better align impact fee mitigation awards with the level of economic benefit generated by a project, while preserving the Board’s discretion to approve, deny, reduce, or condition any incentive award.
The ordinance also establishes enhanced wage expectations, defines “catalytic project,” incorporates the County’s Economic Incentive Scoring Matrix, and requires a minimum score of fifty (50) points for Impact Fee Mitigation eligibility. This higher eligibility floor recognizes that impact fee mitigation directly affects infrastructure funding and should be reserved for projects demonstrating meaningful economic and fiscal benefit to the County.
In addition, the ordinance strengthens fiscal safeguards and accountability by requiring performance agreements, annual compliance documentation, fiscal impact analysis for larger mitigation awards, audit and record retention requirements, and clawback/recapture provisions if a recipient fails to meet performance obligations, relocates outside the County, or ceases operations. These revisions are intended to ensure that impact fee mitigation remains a performance-based economic development tool that supports high-quality job creation, protects public infrastructure funding, and provides a measurable return to the County.

description:
The Board of County Commissioners previously established the Job Growth Investment Grant (JGIG) Program through Resolution No. 94-168 to encourage economic development, job creation, and capital investment within St. Lucie County. The JGIG guidelines were subsequently amended several times, including by Resolution No. 15-042, which allowed participation by locally owned and operated businesses. The proposed resolution revises and consolidates the County’s economic incentive framework to better align incentive awards with measurable public benefits, including high-wage job creation, capital investment, local economic participation, and long-term economic impact.
The subject resolution adopts the St. Lucie County Economic Incentive Scoring Matrix as the primary evaluation tool for County-administered economic development incentives, including the Job Growth Investment Grant, Ad Valorem Tax Exemption, Impact Fee Mitigation, and any other economic development incentives that may be established or amended by the Board. The scoring matrix is intended to create a uniform, transparent, and performance-based framework for evaluating incentive requests and determining maximum award eligibility.
The revised scoring system prioritizes projects that provide higher wages, create significant numbers of new full-time jobs, and generate substantial capital investment. The scoring matrix also recognizes catalytic projects and large-scale job creation, while clarifying that points are not cumulative across tiers within each category and that scoring does not create an entitlement to incentives. Final incentive awards remain subject to Board approval, available funding, program-specific requirements, and project-specific considerations.
The resolution also amends the JGIG Program by tying grant eligibility and maximum award levels directly to the scoring matrix. The JGIG framework retains a base per-job grant value and allows performance-based enhancements for higher wages, major capital investment, research and development activity, local hires, and local contractor participation. The maximum JGIG award for an individual project is established at $2.5 million, unless a higher amount is approved by a supermajority vote of the Board.
In addition, JGIG awards will be administered as performance-based reimbursements rather than upfront payments. Annual payments will be based on verified full-time equivalent jobs created and maintained during the applicable reporting period, with payment schedules reflecting the approved job creation ramp-up. The resolution also establishes annual reporting requirements, a seventy percent (70%) minimum performance threshold for prorated payments, and clawback/recapture provisions allowing the County to require repayment for nonperformance, relocation outside the County, or cessation of operations.
The resolution further adopts the County’s Economic Incentive Application and directs the Planning and Development Services Department, in coordination with the County Attorney’s Office, to administer the incentive program, maintain application and scoring materials, coordinate with the Economic Development Council where appropriate, and monitor compliance. The resolution also recognizes the potential future creation of a separate Locally Owned & Operated Business Incentive (LOOBI) program to provide alternative criteria for qualifying local small businesses, subject to separate implementing criteria and Board approval.
Overall, the proposed amendments are intended to modernize the County’s economic incentive program by increasing transparency, improving consistency across incentive programs, prioritizing higher-wage employment, strengthening fiscal accountability, and ensuring that County incentives are awarded only when tied to verified performance and measurable public benefit.

description:
The Board of County Commissioners previously adopted Resolution No. 03-258 to establish guidelines for the County’s Economic Development Ad Valorem Tax Exemption Program. Since that time, the County’s economic development priorities have evolved, and the existing guidelines no longer fully reflect the County’s current emphasis on high-wage job creation, substantial capital investment, measurable public benefit, and performance-based accountability. The proposed resolution rescinds Resolution No. 03-258 and establishes updated administrative guidelines for the Ad Valorem Tax Exemption Program consistent with Section 196.1995, Florida Statutes, and the County’s existing Ad Valorem Tax Exemption ordinance.
The proposed resolution aligns the Ad Valorem Tax Exemption Program with the County’s broader Economic Incentive Scoring Matrix. Under the revised framework, eligibility and exemption levels are evaluated based on projected and verified job creation, wage levels, and capital investment. The resolution also clarifies that any preliminary evaluation or indication of support for an Ad Valorem Tax Exemption is advisory and does not constitute approval, create vested rights, or replace the required final application process, including submission of Form DR-418 and adoption of a separate tax exemption ordinance by the Board.
The resolution establishes a score-based exemption structure that determines both the maximum exemption percentage and recommended duration of the exemption. Projects scoring in higher tiers may be considered for greater exemption levels and longer exemption terms, while limited-impact projects are expected to receive shorter duration exemptions consistent with reduced public benefit. The recommended exemption schedules are structured on a declining basis and may not exceed ten years, consistent with Florida law. The Board retains full discretion to award less than the maximum exemption, modify the exemption schedule, or deny an exemption based on project-specific considerations and verified public benefit.
The resolution further strengthens fiscal accountability by requiring a Fiscal Impact Analysis for any Ad Valorem Tax Exemption anticipated to generate a cumulative tax benefit exceeding $100,000 over the term of the exemption. The Fiscal Impact Analysis must demonstrate a minimum net fiscal benefit ratio of 1.2 to 1.0 and include projections of net new County revenues and total exemption value, unless waived by the Board upon a specific finding of exceptional public benefit.
In addition to the score-based framework, the resolution requires each approved exemption to be memorialized in a written agreement approved by the Board and in a form approved by the County Attorney. The agreement must include job creation commitments, wage requirements, capital investment commitments, reporting requirements, compliance verification procedures, and clawback/recapture provisions. These requirements are intended to ensure that exemptions are awarded only when tied to measurable commitments and that the County has enforceable remedies in the event of nonperformance.
The resolution also establishes annual compliance and reporting requirements, audit and record retention provisions, and a seventy percent (70%) minimum performance threshold for prorated exemption benefits. If a recipient fails to achieve at least seventy percent of required performance obligations for a reporting period, the exemption benefit for that year is forfeited unless otherwise addressed by the Board. The resolution also provides cure periods for technical defaults and compliance deficiencies, while identifying material defaults such as fraud, intentional misrepresentation, cessation of operations, or sustained performance below required levels.
Finally, the resolution includes strengthened clawback and recapture provisions. The County retains the right to require repayment of incentives in full or on a prorated basis for failure to meet performance obligations, and full repayment is required in the event of relocation outside the County, cessation of operations, or material breach of the agreement. The resolution also provides for debarment from County incentive programs in cases of fraud or misrepresentation and allows interest to accrue on amounts owed.
Overall, the proposed resolution modernizes the County’s Ad Valorem Tax Exemption Program by aligning exemption decisions with the County’s scoring matrix, preserving Board discretion, strengthening fiscal safeguards, requiring annual verification, and ensuring that tax exemptions remain tied to verified public benefit and long-term economic performance.

St. Lucie County will host three Tire Amnesty Events to provide residents a way to recycle unused tires at no cost to them as a way to reduce mosquito breeding, as unused tires stored around yards are notorious for collecting water and becoming prime habitat for disease-carrying mosquito species. • Saturday, May 23 from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. at the St. Lucie County Baling & Recycling Facility, located at 6120 Glades Cut-Off Road in Fort Pierce
• Saturday, May 30 from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. at the Paula Lewis Branch Library, located at 2950 SW Rosser Blvd. in Port St. Lucie

description:
On March 15, 1988, the Board adopted Resolution No. 88-66 establishing the Veterans Advisory Council to serve in an advisory capacity to the Board and to coordinate activities among local veterans organizations. The Council was also intended to function as an informational clearinghouse and provide recommendations regarding veterans-related activities.
The Veterans Advisory Council has not convened since approximately 2012. Since that time, the County’s Veterans Services Division, along with numerous local veterans organizations and community partners, have continued to provide coordination, outreach, and support services to veterans in St. Lucie County.
Given that similar coordination and advisory functions are currently being carried out through existing organizations and partnerships, staff recommends formally sunsetting the Veterans Advisory Council. This action streamlines advisory structures while maintaining the County’s ongoing commitment to supporting veterans through its existing programs and partnerships. The continued existence of an inactive advisory body is no longer necessary to fulfill the intended purpose outlined in Resolution No. 88-66.

description:
On February 18, 2026, responses to RFP No. 26-014, Disaster Debris Monitoring Management and Consultant Services, were opened. Four proposals were received; 469 companies were notified, and 37 RFP documents were distributed.
The purpose of this RFP is for a firm to assist in debris collection during disaster recovery. St. Lucie County seeks to establish contractual arrangements, with at least one (1) primary and up to three (3) additional qualified firms, to provide management services and technical assistance in regard to the monitoring of disaster debris collection on an as-needed basis.
Hurricanes, tornadoes, and other natural and man-made events frequently produce substantial volumes of debris, creating hazardous conditions that impact public health, welfare and safety by obstructing roads, by creating obstacles to safe passage of emergency and essential pedestrian and vehicular traffic, and by notably increasing potential exposure to fire and hazardous materials. To mitigate the hazardous conditions, it is mandatory that there be an early, safe and rapid response to restoring safe and economically viable conditions by the removal of the debris in a prompt and environmentally protective manner.
St. Lucie County Solid Waste will assign a Debris Manager to the debris collection/management project and will establish and staff a Debris Management Center at the St. Lucie County Baling and Recycling Facility. The Debris Management Center will provide a site for overall coordination of the project with the proposer(s) and local, state, and federal agencies. Authorized local, state, and federal agencies will also provide staff to the Debris Management Center to assure a proper level of coordination. The Debris Management Center will be the primary point of contact for the proposer(s).
The response of the selected monitoring proposer(s) to the disaster recovery process must be immediate, rapid and efficient with acceptable cost controls, accountability procedures, written reports and submittals to assure that the County shall have the means to be reimbursed for all eligible disaster recovery costs from appropriate federal, state, and private agencies. Response will typically be activated only in the event of an emergency and in accordance with an awarded contract.
On March 26, 2026, the selection committee evaluated and ranked the proposals that were received. The committee members' scores and ranking for each firm are provided in Attachment A.
The short-listed firms in order of ranking are as follows:Thompson Consulting Services

description:
On January 24, 2023, the Board of County Commissioners approved Resolution No. 2023-006, committing to provide economic incentives for a new manufacturing facility owned by Meyer Utility Structures, LLC, also known as Arcosa. Subsequently, on March 7, 2023, the Board approved Job Growth Investment Grant Agreement No. 23-001 for the creation of 101 new jobs and deferred the fee in lieu of sidewalk construction for a period of up to 12 months.
On February 6, 2024, the Board approved the first amendment to JGIG Agreement No. 23-001, extending the Year One job creation deadline to December 31, 2024, and providing a 12-month extension for the fee in lieu of sidewalk construction. BIE - Ordinance No. 2026-13 - Comprehensive Plan EAR Amendment

description:
The St. Lucie County Comprehensive Plan serves as the County’s primary policy document guiding growth management and development. It establishes policies and identifies public improvements necessary to maintain and enhance quality of life, protect natural resources, and promote sound long-term economic development, while recognizing the diverse needs of the County’s communities and land uses.
Pursuant to Florida law, the County is required to evaluate its Comprehensive Plan every seven (7) years through the Evaluation and Appraisal Review (EAR) process. This process ensures the Plan remains consistent with applicable statutory requirements and responsive to changes in State law and local conditions.
St. Lucie County has completed its EAR-based update and is seeking public input on the proposed amendments. On August 20, 2025, the Planning and Zoning Commission, acting as the Local Planning Agency, reviewed the amendments and recommended approval to the Board of County Commissioners. On September 2, 2025, the Board conducted a transmittal hearing and unanimously voted to transmit the proposed EAR amendments to the State Land Planning Agency and reviewing agencies.
Following review, the State Land Planning Agency (Florida Commerce) issued a letter dated November 10, 2025, identifying five (5) proposed amendments as inconsistent with Chapter 2025-190, Section 28, Laws of Florida (SB 180), on the basis that the provisions were more restrictive or burdensome than the currently adopted Comprehensive Plan. In response, the County removed the identified language and reverted to the existing adopted provisions.
Additionally, the South Florida Water Management District (SFWMD) provided five (5) comments and technical corrections that are required to be addressed prior to final adoption of the EAR amendments. The County addressed the SFWMD comments.
County staff monitored the 2026 legislative session for modifications to the provisions of SB 180. There were no modifications to the existing provisions limiting a local government from adopting more restrictive or burdensome comprehensive plan amendments and/or land development regulations before October 1, 2027. The County's deadline to adopt the EAR amendments is May 9, 2026.
----------------
Pursuant to Section 163.3191, Florida Statutes, local governments are required to evaluate their Comprehensive Plan to determine whether amendments are necessary to reflect changes in state requirements, in accordance with the schedule established by the State Land Planning Agency (Florida Department of Commerce). St. Lucie County was required to notify the Department of Commerce by October 1, 2024, regarding whether updates to the Comprehensive Plan were needed.
On September 19, 2024, the County submitted its notification to the Department of Commerce, identifying that amendments were necessary to address changes in state requirements and noting that additional amendments may be considered to address issues of local concern. Based on this notification, the County was required to transmit any proposed Comprehensive Plan amendments to the Department of Commerce by September 30, 2025.
-----------------
The St. Lucie County Comprehensive Plan consists of fourteen (14) elements and one (1) Port sub-element. As part of the EAR process, the County prepared updates on all elements except for the Rural Lands Stewardship Area Element and the Property Rights Element. The majority of the proposed revisions consist of incorporating statutory updates, removing obsolete text and data, and replacing it with current information.
Within the draft amendments, deletions are shown in strikethrough, and additions are underlined. Revisions made following the Board of County Commissioners transmittal hearing are highlighted in yellow for ease of review.

description:
This agenda item is to request permission to advertise an RFP that solicits proposals from qualified applicants to design, finance, construct, operate and maintain non-aeronautical facilities, specifically a hotel and associated amenities, on approximately 20 acres (the parcel) at the entrance of the Treasure Coast International Airport. The parcel is offered “as-is”. Assessment of the existing parcel conditions is the responsibility of each proposer. The selected proposer, if any, will be required to negotiate an appropriate agreement to lease and develop the parcel (the Lease Agreement), with a term to be agreed upon with the County and commensurate with the proposed level of investment in the parcel and the nature of the proposed development.
------------------
In April 2025, the County received a letter of interest in developing a hotel near the entrance of the Airport.
On May 13, 2025, at the BOCC Informal Meeting, the BOCC received an Airport Update and the BOCC discussed airport activities such as appraisals, rental rates, derelict airplanes, an uninhabitable hangar, and unpermitted construction. No formal direction was provided. This update included the proposal for a hotel.
On July 10, 2025 at the BOCC Informal Meeting, the BOCC received an Airport Private Proposal Update and following the discussion, the Board expressed support and reached consensus to proceed with negotiations and advance the proposed projects. This update included the proposal for a hotel.
In December 2025, the County Attorney’s Office distributed research conducted by outside attorneys (Nelson Mullins) to the commission. The research pertains to the Analysis of County Airport Hotel Leasing Authority Under Section 125.35, Florida Statutes:
Summary of the Analysis: Based on the statutory language, Attorney General guidance, local code provisions, and statewide procurement precedent, the proposed hotel must be competitively procured .
On February 10, 2026, at the BOCC Informal meeting, the BOCC discussed the April 2025 letter of interest received to develop a hotel near the entrance of the Airport. The Board discussed the need for the hotel property to go out for RFP.
The minutes for the February 10, 2026 Informal Meeting, approved by the BOCC on March 3, 2026, include: "Upon discussion of the Board, a consensus was reached on issuing the RFP, allowing the Board two weeks for comments/review of the drafted RFP and bringing it back for the final scope/review approval. The RFP will be broadcast/advertised for 90 days, and the consensus is for the Board to serve as the selection committee."
On the March 3, 2026 BOCC Regular meeting, the BOCC approved an agenda ratifying the BOCC direction from the February 10th Informal Meeting. This agenda items included: "20 acres (non-aeronautical use for a Hotel): Staff will share a draft RFP for the BOCC's review and comment. This step may take 15 days for BOCC review. Staff will update the RFP as needed. Depending on the consistency of comments provided, this step may take 25 days to incorporate the comments and confirm changes with Board members....Upon completion of review and receipt of the appraisal, the RFP will be issued and advertised for 90 days to receive a sealed proposal from respondents.
The BOCC will sit as the selection committee and review the received proposals based on the requirements set forth in the RFP. The selection committee may determine that interviews with the respondents are warranted to further evaluate the submission. The selection committee will provide a decision on the proposals and staff will prepare the agenda item to document the decision. It is anticipated the selection committee review process and the agenda item may take up to 60 days. Upon BOCC approval of the recommendation, staff will initiate negotiations and seek to complete lease agreements within 90 days."
The draft RFP was shared with the BOCC on March 19, 2026, for review and comment. The draft RFP document was updated based on comments received for this permission to advertise. This is in alignment with Strategic Plan Objectives ECON 2.4.3 and TC 5.2.4.

description:
The State Housing Initiatives Partnership (SHIP) Program, established under sections 420.907–420.9079, Florida Statutes, requires local governments to adopt and maintain a Local Housing Assistance Plan (LHAP outlining the strategies through which SHIP funds will be used to address local affordable housing needs. On May 6, 2025, the Board of County Commissioners approved the current three-year LHAP for Fiscal Years 2025–2026, 2026–2027, and 2027–2028.
Since adoption of the LHAP, the Community Services Department, Housing Division, has continued to evaluate housing market conditions and emerging needs among income-eligible households. As part of this review, staff identified the need to include a foreclosure prevention strategy to help stabilize homeowners experiencing temporary financial hardship and reduce the risk of displacement. Rising housing costs, insurance premiums, and other economic pressures have increased the likelihood that otherwise stable households may fall behind on mortgage payments.
The proposed foreclosure prevention strategy allows for one-time assistance to eligible homeowners to cure mortgage delinquencies on fully amortizing, fixed-rate first mortgages. Assistance may be used for delinquent principal, interest, escrow shortages, late fees, and lender-required reinstatement costs, subject to a maximum award amount and strict eligibility criteria. Households must demonstrate a qualifying hardship, provide documentation of arrearage, complete housing counseling, and show the ability to resume mortgage payments following assistance. The strategy is designed as a short-term intervention to preserve homeownership and prevent avoidable foreclosures.
The Florida Housing Finance Corporation reviewed the proposed foreclosure prevention strategy and issued conditional approval on December 17, 2025. Final approval is contingent upon adoption of the amendment by the Board of County Commissioners and submission of the amended LHAP with an executed resolution. Approval of the attached resolution will formally amend the LHAP to include the foreclosure prevention strategy and authorize submission of the required documentation for final approval, consistent with SHIP program requirements.
This item supports the County’s Strategic Plan, specifically Objective HS 6.4.1 – Provide economic stability and support services in our community for those individuals and families experiencing vulnerabilities.

description:
Nine years ago, Tom Rhodes, owner of Sunshine Laundry, volunteered at a Free Laundry event in Atlanta, Georgia. At the event, free laundry and drying services were given to everyone who attended the event. While everyone was appreciative, one woman in particular was overcome with emotion at the kind gesture. The woman explained that drowning is a high percentage of accidental deaths in African American children in the United States. She told Mr. Rhodes she was going to use the $15.00 she saved on laundry and use it to pay for swim lessons for her son.
The encounter sparked an idea for Mr. Rhodes. He decided to return to St. Lucie County and do something to help children learn to swim. By offering swim lessons, he hopes those who do not know how to swim will learn to appreciate the water and be safer at the pool or beach.
From 2017 to 2019, Sunshine Laundry donated $2,000.00 each year to sponsor children or adults to receive American Red Cross Swim Lessons at all St. Lucie County Pools. From 2021-2023, Sunshine Laundry donated $2500.00 towards swim lessons. In 2024 and 2025, Sunshine Laundry has donated $2,750.00 to provide scholarships for these swim lessons. These funds provided 50 individuals with lessons. This year, 2026, Sunshine Laundry is donating $1,650.00 for swimming lessons, less amount of money than previous years due to leftover funds from 2025. The cost of the lessons is $75.00 per participant. Sunshine Laundry's contribution will provide a $55.00 scholarship to 30 participants. These participants will be responsible for the remaining $20.00. Mr. Tom Rhodes, of Sunshine Laundry, is in attendance to present a check to the Board of County Commissioners.

attachments.name: Resolution 10-060 Expediting Review of Affordable Housing Projects

description:
On March 9, 2010, the Board of County Commissioners adopted Resolution No. 10-060, directing the St. Lucie County Building Official to expedite the review of building permit applications for affordable housing projects receiving County-administered grant funding.
Since that time, state housing policy and local housing needs have continued to evolve. The Affordable Housing Advisory Committee (AHAC), pursuant to Section 420.9076, Florida Statutes, reviewed the County’s existing policies and recommended updates to ensure alignment with current statutory requirements and to further reduce regulatory barriers to affordable housing development.
The proposed resolution repeals and replaces Resolution No. 10-060 to clarify and expand eligibility for expedited building permit review. In addition to projects receiving County housing funds, the updated policy includes projects that provide housing subject to recorded and enforceable affordability or income-restriction requirements. Eligibility must be demonstrated through objective documentation such as regulatory agreements, land use restrictions, deed restrictions, or funding award letters confirming restricted rents or sales prices and applicable income thresholds.
The resolution also defines “expedited review” to mean prioritizing qualifying applications in the review process and advancing them ahead of non-qualifying applications to the maximum extent practicable, including the use of concurrent or parallel review where feasible.
These updates are consistent with Sections 420.9071 and 420.9076, Florida Statutes, which require local governments participating in the State Housing Initiatives Partnership (SHIP) Program to expedite the processing of development orders and permits for affordable housing. Additionally, the revisions align with the intent of the Live Local Act (Senate Bill 102, 2023), which emphasizes the role of local governments in implementing streamlined and expedited permitting processes to support the development of workforce and income-restricted housing.
Approval of this resolution will provide greater clarity and consistency in the County’s expedited permitting process and support the timely development of affordable housing throughout St. Lucie County.
This request aligns with the following strategic plan initiatives: ECON 2.1.4 – Support the development of housing for all income levels of the workforce to assist with the attraction and retention of talent.
TC 5.3.1 – Promote and encourage a mix of housing types to address affordable, essential and workforce housing needs.
TC 5.3.4 – Develop community-based strategies to address homelessness and unsheltered.
TC 5.3.5 – Seek out and leverage state and federal funding sources to expand the housing inventory and improve housing affordability.
meeting: Board of County Commissioners Regular Meeting

description:
The design of the Selvitz Road Widening project utilizes an alternate Glades Cut Off Road alignment that will extend through multiple parcels and run parallel to the Carriage Pointe subdivision. The new alignment requires the purchase of an approximate 3.92 +/- acre strip of land east of Ralls Road and west of Selvitz Road from Glen R. Stevick, as Trustee for the Glen Cove Self Directed Trust. (Parcel ID 2430-411-0002-000-3) The design for this project is approximately 60% complete, and the County is continuing to coordinate with all impacted property owners.
In 2025, the County had an appraisal prepared by Callaway and Price, Inc. that valued the right-of-way tract at $444,000.00. Mr. Stevick’s contracted appraiser, Valbridge Property Advisors, valued the right-of-way at $530,000.00. The County’s contracted appraiser, Boyle & Drake, Inc., reviewed the County and the Seller’s appraisals and deemed the County’s appraisal as acceptable. The County submitted an offer of $444,000.00 to Mr. Stevick’s representative. Mr. Stevick’s representative submitted a counteroffer of $530,000.00. The County has attempted to negotiate the sale of this property at the appraised value for an extended period of time. The project design and construction schedule would be severely impacted by seeking an alternative route that could possibly eliminate or reduce the need for right-of-way from Mr. Stevick’s property. Therefore, it is the opinion of Public Works that negotiating an offer higher than the County’s appraised value is in the best interest of the County.
In an eminent domain proceeding, the County is responsible for payment of both its own attorneys’ fees and expert witness costs as well as attorneys’ fees and expert witness costs for the property owner. In consideration of the potential cost exposure to the County, staff has accepted Mr. Stevick's counteroffer of $530,000.00.
Attached for your review and approval is the signed Contract for Sale and Purchase.

description:
The Environmental Resources Department (ERD) is working toward the goal of acquiring lots within a 486-acre subdivided area northwest of Turnpike Feeder Road that contains approximately 215 lots total. The area is identified in the 2004 SLC Native Habitat Inventory as an “A” based on high-quality native habitat coverage and potential for rare or endemic species. Approximately 115 lots have already been acquired. County staff has been monitoring the area to determine if any properties are available. On May 4, 2026, three parcels will be offered for bid in a Tax Deed Auction. These parcels total 1.52 acres and are located adjacent to Turnpike Feeder Road and southwest of US Highway 1. In recent appraisals of the adjacent land-locked parcels, a value of $7,500 was identified. Tax Deed 25-451 - Parcel I.D. No. 1406-324-0003-000-5 - .52 acres - Starting Bid - $1,484.23
Tax Deed 25-452 - Parcel I.D. No. 1406-333-0016-000-7 - .49 acres - Starting Bid - $1,638.47
Tax Deed 26-004 - Parcel I.D. No. 1407-211-0014-000-1 - .51 acres - Starting Bid - $1,700.50
As part of the Tax Deed Application process, the Clerk's Office orders a Property Information Report. Upon review of the reports dated January 23, January 26, and February 13, 2026, there do not appear to be any title defects that may affect County ownership. A search of the Clerk's Official Records did not reveal any liens or judgments. The County has performed Phase I Environmental Assessments on several recent acquisitions north and south of the subject parcels.
By acquiring these parcels through a Tax Deed Auction, staff can reduce the cost to taxpayers by eliminating the need for an appraisal, title commitment and associated closing costs, and environmental assessments. The County must submit a maximum bid for each tax deed auction. The tax deed software automatically bids the auction at $100 increments until the highest maximum bid is reached, and gives the opportunity for last minute bidders to submit a counter-bid should they have sufficient deposit funds. If there is no counter-bidder, the County would be declared the auction winner at the starting bid.
Discussion
In the event the Board determines to authorize the County to bid at the public tax deed auction on the three Turnpike Feeder parcels, County staff has determined that the County will need to take the following statutory steps:The County must register before the public sale
The County must deposit 5% of the County's highest bid with the Clerk prior to the public sale
If the County is the successful (i.e. highest) bidder, the County must deposit the balance of the purchase proceeds by 2:00 p.m. on the day after the public sale (in this case by May 5, 2026 at 2:00 p.m.)

When the 911 Communications Center receives a call requiring fire or emergency medical services (ambulance), the call is immediately transferred to the Fire District’s dispatch center. The dispatcher then assigns the nearest available fire station to respond.
An integrated interface between the 911 Communications Center and Fire Stations enables the electronic transfer of essential call information to the appropriate station. This information is subsequently printed for the specific service required for either fire or emergency medical responses, ensuring that responding Fire District personnel receive accurate and timely details for each call.

Amendments No. 4 and No. 5 were both net zero budget amendments that had no overall budget increases. These amendments clarified certain line items within the Schedule of Values involving various tasks and allowances in order to correctly track invoicing and payments. These were both executed through Administration.
On July 22, 2025, The Board approved Amendment No. 6 to the July 18, 2023 Contract in the amount of $12,186,964.00. That amendment included three pipelines in and around the Tropicana wastewater facility as well as the interim headworks for the current facility. The scope also included the construction of two additional Upper Florida Aquifer (UFA) raw water wells (UFA-1 and UFA-3) at the Central Water Treatment Plant.
Amendment No. 7 was another net zero budget amendment that had no overall budget increase. That amendment clarified allowance and contingency line items.

description:
St. Lucie County Solid Waste (SLCSW) is requesting Board approval to proceed with roofing repairs at the Solid Waste Tipping and Baling Floor and the Solid Waste Administration Building. Due to the age and condition of the roofs, unforeseen conditions—such as wet insulation or deteriorated wood nailers—may be discovered during construction. To address these potential issues, staff is requesting approval of a standard 10% contingency, bringing the total not-to-exceed amount to $1,207,976.00.

description:
On November 27, 2023, the St. Lucie County Board of County Commissioners (“BOCC”) adopted Ordinance No. 2023-18, amending the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan to establish the P1 Motor Club Special District (“P1MC”) with regulating standards for a private mixed-use motorsports complex.
On August 5, 2025, the BOCC adopted Ordinance No. 2025-17, amending the P1MC Special District Regulatory Standards to provide that the project may be served by either a privately provided, self-contained water system or by public water service from the St. Lucie County Utility District (“District”), with the intent that any such service be provided at no net cost to the County.
On December 3, 2025, the County issued a Utility Service Availability Status Letter to P1MC Landowners, LLC (“Property Owner”), outlining a non-binding framework under which potable water service could be provided through a privately owned transmission main connecting to a metered point within the District’s Utility Service Area, with the Property Owner bearing responsibility for the transmission infrastructure.
Subsequent coordination with the Florida Department of Transportation (“FDOT”) has identified a permitting constraint affecting that approach. FDOT requires that utility infrastructure located within its right-of-way be permitted to and owned by a qualifying utility entity. As a result, the privately owned transmission main concept described in the December 3, 2025, Utility Service Availability Status Letter is not presently feasible and an alternative service framework must be considered.
Staff has evaluated a potential alternative under which the District would serve as the permittee for portions of the transmission main within FDOT right-of-way and such facilities, as approved by the District, may be incorporated into the District’s system. Under this general approach, the Property Owner would remain responsible for funding the design and construction of the transmission facilities and for reimbursing the District for costs attributable to service to the project, subject to the terms of negotiated agreements.
The transmission facilities are intended solely to serve P1MC and will not be made available for service connections by other properties, except as may be determined by the District in its sole discretion.
Staff is seeking the District's authorization to negotiate a Bulk Water Purchase Agreement and any related agreements necessary to implement a revised service framework for Property Owner. Any such agreements will be structured to ensure that (i) Property Owner bears financial responsibility for project-related infrastructure and associated costs, and (ii) the County and District are protected from unreimbursed capital, operational, and regulatory costs.
No final agreement is being approved at this time. Any negotiated agreements will be brought back for review and approval.

description:
In early September 2025, Public Works was alerted to a small hole and pavement depression in the southbound left turn lane of Sunrise Boulevard at Edwards Road. An initial inspection by Engineering staff and a local contractor revealed that gaps between segments of a 66-inch concrete stormwater pipe had caused erosion of the foundation soils beneath the roadway. To temporarily stabilize the area and ensure public safety, a concrete slurry mixture was poured into the hole. Ground penetrating radar (GPR) was used to further assess the subsurface conditions. While no large voids were detected, the scan revealed pockets of very loose, saturated soil along the pipe, confirming that the subgrade conditions posed a significant safety risk.
Staff determined that immediate action was necessary to prevent further erosion and potential collapse of the travel lane. Public Works requested emergency administrative approval to proceed with repairs under the County’s Emergency Purchase protocol. PRP Construction Group, LLC, was selected to perform the necessary repairs and pavement restoration using available funds from the Stormwater Management Fund Reserve fund. The emergency repairs included sealing the pipe joints and densifying the surrounding soil to restore the structural integrity of the roadway.
The construction budget was:
Proposal: $128,050.00
5% Contingency: $ 0.00
Total Construction Budget $128,050.00
The project was completed on budget with a remaining amount of $0.00. There were no change orders during the project.
Staff monitored the construction and determined the project was completed in conformance with the plans and specifications.
