description:
Lennar Homes, LLC is proposing a rezoning amendment for +/-1,027 acres from AG-1 (Agricultural-1) to PUD (Planned Unit Development) & Preliminary Development Plan, for the Indrio Groves Hamlet PUD. The property has a future land use designation of TVC (Towns, Villages and Countryside). The Applicant proposes a Hamlet PUD within the TVC Overlay including up to 3,081 dwellings, a childcare center, a future K-8 school site, commercial and civic space, at least forty percent (40%) open space, dedication of right-of-way, construction of roads, extension of water and sanitary sewer lines, and other related improvements.
A Hamlet PUD became a development option outside the Urban Services Boundary in the Towns, Villages and Countryside Future Land Use category in the autumn of 2024 when amendments to the Comprehensive Plan and the Land Development Code took effect. The option of rezoning to PUD (Planned Unit Development) was added to the option of rezoning to PTV (Planned Towns and Villages) if increased density is desired, or rezoning to PCS (Planned Country Subdivision), if development with the density recognized by the Transferable Development Value Map was desired.
Pursuant to the adopted Comprehensive Plan policies and the LDC, residential density may be increased from 1 dwelling unit per acre (DU/A) (as provided in the Transferable Development Value Map) to 3 DU/A by providing 10% workforce housing that remains affordable for at least 20 years or 9% workforce housing and a child care center on-site. The minimum amount of open space can be reduced from sixty percent (60%) to forty percent (40%) by the inclusion of open space that is available for active and passive recreation within 1/4 mile of a majority of the residents, civic spaces, and at least one local store to support the daily needs of residents. Density can also be increased to 3 DU/A through the acquisition of transferable development credits, but acquisition of transferable development credits is not required.

description:
At the February 10, 2026 Informal Meeting, the Board of County Commissioners discussed various airport property and provided guidance on next steps to staff for the leasing of parcels within the Treasure Coast International Airport. The specific guidance for each location is as follows:
US 1 Parcels (3163 and 3175 N U.S. Hwy. 1): Acquire appraisals for each parcel individually and for the entirety of the land (combined parcels) and provide the appraised value for both leasing and selling the parcels. Staff to explore the process and timing to receive approval from the FDOT to surplus/sell the property and to receive approval from the FAA for the disposal of airport lands. Staff to provide the values to the BOCC for review and seek direction to either lease or seek approval to sell the parcels.
Aero East (parcels A, B, C, D, E & F): Acquire updated appraisals for the Aero East parcels. This step may take up to 90 days. Staff will update and prepare an RFP for qualified applicants to submit proposals to develop and operate aeronautical facilities on one or more undeveloped parcels of land on Aero East. This step may take up to 15-25 days. Staff will provide the updated RFP to the BOCC for review and comment. This step may take 15 days for BOCC review. Staff will update the RFP as needed. Depending on the consistency of comments provided, this step may take up to 15 days.
Upon completion of review and receipt of the appraisal, the RFP will be issued and advertised for 45 days to receive a sealed proposal from respondents. A selection committee will review the received proposals based on the requirements set forth in the RFP. The selection committee may determine that interviews with the respondents are warranted to further evaluate the submission. The selection committee will provide a recommendation, which is provided to the BOCC via an agenda item for their review and approval. It is anticipated the selection committee review process and the presentation of a recommendation to the BOCC may take up to 60 days. Upon BOCC action, assuming approval of the recommendation, staff will initiate negotiations and seek to complete lease agreements within 90 days.
In total, this competitive solicitation process is anticipated to take about 1 year.
Aero West (parcels E & F): Acquire updated appraisals for the Aero West parcels. This step may take up to 90 days. Staff will update and prepare an RFP for qualified applicants to submit proposals to develop and operate aeronautical facilities on one or both undeveloped parcels of land on Aero West. This step may take up to 15-25 days. Staff will provide the updated RFP to the BOCC for review and comment. This step may take 15 days for BOCC review. Staff will update the RFP as needed. Depending on the consistency of comments provided, this step may take up to 15 days.
Upon completion of review and receipt of the appraisal, the RFP will be issued and advertised for 45 days to receive a sealed proposal from respondents. A selection committee will review the received proposals based on the requirements set forth in the RFP. The selection committee may determine that interviews with the respondents are warranted to further evaluate the submission. The selection committee will provide a recommendation, which is provided to the BOCC via an agenda item for their review and approval. It is anticipated the selection committee review process and the presentation of a recommendation to the BOCC may take up to 60 days. Upon BOCC action, assuming approval of the recommendation, staff will initiate negotiations and seek to complete lease agreements within 90 days.
In total, this competitive solicitation process is anticipated to take about 1 year.
90 acres: Staff is directed to continue direct negotiations with Gulfstream Building Group for aeronautical uses, as the BOCC finds extenuating circumstances with the proposal including the dedication of additional land to the airport. The BOCC direction includes that the negotiations and lease agreement must include the incorporation of the privately-owned, approx. 71.49 acre parcel (1430-231-0001-000-1) into the Airport (becomes County property). Assuming the property owner agrees to the transition of land, an appraisal will be needed to determine the fair market value. This step may take up to 90 days. Upon receipt of the appraisal, staff will attempt to complete a lease agreement within 90 days.
In total, this process is anticipated to take about 6 to 9 months, as the acquisition and incorporation of the private 71.49 acre parcel will include FAA reviews and environmental site assessments. If needed, at the 6 month timeframe, staff will update the BOCC and seek direction on additional time to complete the lease agreement based on the due diligence and environmental review process.
20 acres (non-aeronautical use for a Hotel): Staff will share a draft RFP for the BOCC's review and comment. This step may take 15 days for BOCC review. Staff will update the RFP as needed. Depending on the consistency of comments provided, this step may take 25 days to incorporate the comments and confirm changes with Board members.
The FAA Compliance Guidance Letter 2018-3, Appraisal Standards for the Sale and Disposal of Federally Obligated Airport Property states that "in general, for FAA review of sale or lease of properties, if a matter has not gone to contract one year from the date of submission of the appraisal, then a new appraisal report is needed." As such, the County will likely need to acquire an updated appraisal and this step may take up to 90 days.
Upon completion of review and receipt of the appraisal, the RFP will be issued and advertised for 90 days to receive a sealed proposal from respondents. The BOCC will sit as the selection committee and review the received proposals based on the requirements set forth in the RFP. The selection committee may determine that interviews with the respondents are warranted to further evaluate the submission. The selection committee will provide a decision on the proposals and staff will prepare the agenda item to document the decision. It is anticipated the selection committee review process and the agenda item may take up to 60 days. Upon BOCC approval of the recommendation, staff will initiate negotiations and seek to complete lease agreements within 90 days.
In total, this competitive solicitation process is anticipated to take a little over 1 year.
Airport West Commerce Park (non-aeronautical): Staff is directed to follow the bid/proposal waiver procedure in Section 32-133 of the Code of Ordinances. This process will require:(1) Publish a notice in a newspaper of general circulation in the county at least ten days before the board's regular meeting at which the bid or proposal waiver will be considered. The notice shall identify the nature of the proposed bid or proposal waiver and shall identify the county office where copies of the draft resolution providing for the bid or proposal waiver may be reviewed or obtained. The notice shall also provide the time and manner for persons making objections in writing or otherwise.
(2) Consider the proposed waiver as a regular (non-consent) agenda item at a regularly scheduled board meeting. Although the item is not a public hearing, interested members of the public may comment on the item during general public comment or at the time the item is presented.
(3) Adopt a resolution specifying the basis for the competitive bid waiver in the event the board determines to grant the waiver.
Upon completion of the waiver procedure, staff will continue direct negotiations with Gulfstream Building Group for targeted industries meeting the criteria in Section 24-1 of the Code of Ordinances.
The FAA Compliance Guidance Letter 2018-3, Appraisal Standards for the Sale and Disposal of Federally Obligated Airport Property states that "in general, for FAA review of sale or lease of properties, if a matter has not gone to contract one year from the date of submission of the appraisal, then a new appraisal report is needed." As such, the County will likely need to acquire an updated appraisal and this step may take up to 90 days.
With the updated appraisal, staff will seek to complete lease agreements within 90 days.
In total, this process is anticipated to take about 6 months.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
As a note, the Purchasing Policy Procedures Manual approved by the BOCC in December 2025 provides that in RFPs: "Local businesses which meet all of the criteria for a local business as set forth in this article shall be given a preference in the amount of five percent of the total score of the local business" and further states that "The provisions of this policy shall not apply where prohibited by federal or Florida law or where prohibited under the conditions of any grant....The provisions of this policy shall not be applied to any procurement where the local nature of a business has been addressed through scoring criteria."

attachments.name: Johnston Rd Box Culverts_PRP CO1 Proposal_2-17-26

description:
On August 5, 2025, the Board approved award of Bid 25-034 to PRP Construction Group, LLC for the Johnston Road at Fort Pierce Farms Water Control District (FPFWCD) Canals C-16 and C-17 Culvert Replacement project in the amount of $1,398,913.45. The project includes the replacement of two failing 84-inch metal culvert pipes with concrete box culverts under Johnston Road north of the Meadowood Country Club community. The scope of work also includes removing and replacing eight side drains that will be connected to the box culverts, armoring the canal banks with rip rap rubble for erosion protection, and maintaining existing drainage. Additional tasks include guardrail removal and replacement, side slope restoration, roadway reconstruction, removal and replacement of fencing, and the restoration and installation of signage, pavement markings, and sod.
Johnston Road must be closed during a portion of the construction. The closure is anticipated to last up to three months, during which time a large crane will be used to install the heavy concrete box culvert sections under the road. The contractor has procured the precast concrete materials and is prepared to start work immediately, but has not mobilized equipment to the jobsite.
Due to unsafe conditions resulting from a collapsed culvert pipe beneath the roadway, Johnston Road was closed on October 22, 2025. Johnston Road was closed approximately 1/2 mile south of Indrio Road at the crossing of Canals 1 and 15 for an emergency project to repair a damaged pipe crossing that created a cavity in the road. This closure was unanticipated and staff worked as quickly as possible to complete the repair using emergency procurement procedures. The road was re-opened to traffic on February 12, 2026, a total closure duration of approximately 16 weeks. PRP Construction Group, LLC worked with the County during this time and agreed not to begin construction, as 2 simultaneous closures would have landlocked certain properties and isolated them from access.
The project location (C25-08-748) and the location of the unanticipated culvert collapse are depicted below.
Additionally, the necessary road detour due to the unanticipated culvert collapse is depicted below.
A business owner located southeast of the emergency closure, which depends on both residents and tourists, states that they were impacted by the reduced accessibility due to the road detour. Travelers who would normally pass through the area were forced to take a lengthy detour via Kings Highway and Angle Road, leading to fewer customers and affecting business operations, according to the owner. Staff have worked to accommodate the business owner using messaging and signage to support enhanced wayfinding during the detour.
The business owner has now approached County staff with concerns about business impacts for the planned Canal 16 and 17 project due to closing Johnston Road during the business owner's high season (winter and spring) and has requested that the construction be postponed until June.
To evaluate the business owner’s request, staff requested a cost estimate to postpone until June. The contractor has submitted a change order in the amount of $49,900.00 to postpone the work. The large concrete box culverts would be delivered and stored in the County right of way near the project site. Because the materials that have been procured are high-value items, part of this amendment would include adding language to the County's standard contract to allow for payment of stored materials, specifically, box culverts and sheet piling. This provision is logical to not require a large cash-flow outlay by the contractor if the Board supports the added costs. Staff have reviewed the cost proposal and finds it reflective of the additional costs associated with renting a crane a second time and double-handling the large concrete material.
This project is being completed in accordance with Strategic Plan provision QI 3.1.1

attachments.name: First Amendment to Ground Lease Agreement - Finnish Strong

description:
The Finnish Strong, LLC (Aircraft Turbine Works) original lease agreement (C24-08-1135) was executed on June 2, 2025 for the lease of Parcels A and B within Areo West. Since execution of the lease, a discrepancy in the land area for a drainage feature has been discovered. The land area in the lease is decreasing from 189,458.17 square feet to 172,247.11 square feet, with a corresponding decrease in rent and rent credit of $152.98/month for nine months. The amendment further updates Section 10.2 from a three-party agreement with 1/3 of the water main cost to a reimbursement agreement with 1/4 of the water main cost, as there is an additional potential lessee in Aero West.
In 2024, the County issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 24-055, Develop Aero West Parcels at Treasure Coast International Airport. Aero West consisted of six parcels totaling approximately 13 acres. The intent for this RFP was for qualified applicants to submit proposals to develop and operate aeronautical facilities on one or more undeveloped parcels of land on Aero West.
On July 17, 2024, responses to RFP No. 24-055, included a sole proposal in response to RFP No. 24-055. Aircraft Turbine Works for Parcel A (686 companies were notified, and 53 RFP documents were distributed). Aircraft Turbine Works proposal included a phased approach, beginning with the construction of one 12,000 square foot hangar and 3,600 square feet of office space on approximately 2 acres on Parcel A.
On August 8, 2024, the selection committee evaluated the proposal from Aircraft Turbine Works and determined that the proposal was responsive and made a recommendation to move forward with negotiations. On August 27, 2024, the Board approved the selection committee recommendation for RFP No. 24-055 and permission to conduct contract negotiations with Aircraft Turbine Works; and if negotiations were successful, award the contract to Aircraft Turbine Works. County staffed engaged with Aircraft Turbine Works to negotiate a lease. Through the negotiations, Aircraft Turbine Works requested to add Parcel B to their proposal and build a second hangar and office. In June of 2025, the County entered into a lease agreement with Aircraft Turbine Works (Finnish Strong LLC).
The proposed lease amendment is in alignment with Strategic Plan Objectives ECON 2.4.3 and ECON 2.1.1.

description:
The County has completed the sealed bid process for BID No. 25-076, Veteran Shelter Renovation Project. Bid responses were opened on January 14, 2026. As a result of this solicitation, two bids were received following notification to sixty-two (62) companies and distribution of six hundred thirty-one (631) bid documents.
After review, FSV Construction Company was determined to be the lowest responsive and responsible bidder with a total project cost of $817,259.56. This amount includes the base bid, a ten percent (10%) contingency, permit allowance, cost of the public construction bond, and selected alternates. The alternates consist of the addition of a roof-covered structure for new pump equipment, striping and repainting sidewalks, and installation of a galvanized sleeve in lieu of stainless steel.
This renovation project supports the conversion of the County-owned property located at 3455 U.S. Highway 1 in Fort Pierce into a shelter for homeless veterans and represents a key implementation step following completion of architectural and engineering design. In January 2025, the Board approved a work authorization with Song + Associates, Inc. for architectural design, permitting, bidding assistance, and construction administration services for the Veterans Homeless Shelter project. In September 2025, signed plans were received from the architect and a project manual was received in October 2025. An Invitation to Bid for the construction was issued on November 2, 2025. The construction bid due date was January 14, 2026.
Award of this bid will allow construction to proceed and advances the County’s ongoing efforts to expand supportive housing options for veterans in the community.
This item supports the FY2026–FY2030 Strategic Plan by advancing Thriving Community and Health & Safety objectives, including TC 5.3.3, TC 5.3.4, and HS 6.4.1, through coordination with community partners to expand stable housing solutions for veterans, implementation of community-based strategies to address homelessness and unsheltered populations, and provision of economic stability and support services for vulnerable individuals and families.

description:
The Library is requesting Board approval to authorize the Chair to execute a subscription agreement with McNaughton for the Adult Lease Plan, which replaces the Library’s prior lease agreement with Baker & Taylor. This action is necessary due to the closure of Baker & Taylor’s leasing program, which previously provided the Library with a steady supply of high-demand adult titles through a rotating lease collection.
Lease collections are a critical component of the Library’s materials strategy. They allow the Library to provide patrons with access to current, high-interest titles without permanently adding all items to the circulating collection. This model supports strong customer service by reducing wait times for popular materials while also addressing space limitations within library facilities. Because leased items are returned and refreshed on a regular cycle, the Library can maintain a dynamic, up-to-date collection without increasing long-term shelving and storage demands.
The McNaughton subscription offers a comparable leasing structure that ensures continuity of service following the Baker & Taylor closure. Approval of this agreement will allow the Library to continue meeting patron demand for new adult materials in a fiscally responsible and space-efficient manner.

attachments.name: Notification from Clerk of Circuit Court

description:
The Property Acquisition Division received notification from the Clerk of the Circuit Court that Parcel ID 2429-441-0005-010-6 was subject to a Tax Deed Sale on October 6, 2025. There were no bidders and the 0.16 acre parcel had been placed on the List of Lands Available. We contacted the Environmental Resources Department (ERD) to see if there was an interest in acquiring this parcel based on its location to Five Mile Creek.
ERD determined they are interested in acquiring this parcel due to several factors including:
• Most of the site consists of mixed native upland and wetland habitats (floodplain forest and hydric hammock dominated by live oaks, laurel oaks, and cabbage palms).
• The primary land acquisition goal of the Environmentally Significant Lands program has always been to acquire and preserve the high-quality native habitats located along the North Fork of the St. Lucie River (NFSLR) and their tributaries, Five and Ten Mile Creeks.
• This site would not require much management as it is already high-quality native habitat with few non-native invasive species. Management would consist primarily of non-native invasive species removal and potentially hydrologic restoration if a need is identified.
• A secondary goal would be providing passive recreational opportunities such as connectivity to the SLC Greenways & Paddling Trail corridors.
• The parcel is adjacent to Five Mile Creek and would protect 78 linear feet of shoreline.
• The parcel is directly adjacent to a strip of land to the north of approximately 600 linear feet long abutting 25th Street to the east and Five Mile Creek to the west. This connectivity could potentially facilitate public access such as a nature trail or potentially kayak launch.
• The parcel is adjacent to the 138-acre Miller Preserve directly across Five Mile Creek. This connectivity could potentially facilitate public access such as a nature trail from 25th Street to a pedestrian bridge across Five Mile Creek connecting to the Miller Preserve.
• The parcel is located within the regulatory floodway and the AE flood zone and will assist the County in maintaining its class rating in FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) Community Rating System (CRS) which provides flood insurance discounts for our community, with our comprehensive floodplain management and the protection of the floodplain.

description:
St. Lucie County Solid Waste (SLCSW) requests approval to purchase a CAT 270 Skid Steer Loader through Florida Sheriffs State Bid No. FSA23-EQU21.1 (Equipment).
This equipment is required to support daily landfill operations involving material handling and bale processing. The CAT 270 Skid Steer Loader will improve operational efficiency by consolidating the functions of two existing machines—a forklift and a skid steer—both of which are nearing the end of their useful service lives.
The proposed purchase will allow SLCSW to replace the aging forklift and reduce the need for multiple operators, effectively freeing one SLCSW employee to be reassigned to other essential duties. This consolidation will increase productivity, reduce operational inefficiencies, and provide a reliable long-term equipment solution. The CAT 270 Skid Steer Loader will be used to load debris onto the baling conveyor, load and unload completed bales, and clean the baling floor.
This request is in alignment with Strategic initiative QI 3.1.5 – Perform regular reviews of county facilities and fleet for suitability of use, looking at modifications to improve safety, function and cost-effectiveness.

description:
The areas around Lennard Road east of Prima Vista and Tilton Road have challenging drainage conditions that worsen after significant storm events. To benefit the overall watershed, the County aims to implement drainage improvements along Tilton Road and Silver Oak Drive, which will involve designing and permitting an enhanced stormwater collection/conveyance system within the existing County roadway right-of-way. The Silver Oak PUD project conveyed property to the County in the southeast quadrant of the Dyer Road/Silver Oak Drive intersection for a future Lennard Road alignment and future stormwater management facilities to provide additional basin storage. All work will occur within County-owned right-of-way and property.
Phase 1 of the project was awarded on March 7, 2023, with Final Acceptance on October 1, 2024. Phase I came in $2,172,319 under budget, allowing an opportunity to reallocate these funds towards the completion of Phase 2 of the project. ​
Phase 2 was advertised on November 2, 2025, and the bid opening was on December 17, 2025. Fifteen bidders submitted, and the lowest apparent bidder was Trans Florida Development from Miami, FL. The lowest apparent bid price was submitted at $4,807,582.46. However, upon checking references, it was determined that the information could not be verified. Therefore, the submittal from Trans Florida was deemed non-responsive.
The second-lowest bidder was Dickerson Infrastructure dba Dickerson Florida from Fort Pierce, FL at $4,875,195.77, which is approximately 1.4% higher than the apparent low bid. Staff checked the references submitted by Dickerson Florida and they were verified.
Staff recommends establishment of the project budget as follows:Construction: $4,875,195.77 (includes 10% contingency)
CEI and Materials Testing: $595,510 (already under contract)
Total: $5,470,705.77

attachments.name: Approved Agenda Item 10.H.1 - RFP Art Conservator Services

description:
This is part of the Art in Public Places program established by County Ordinance on July 6, 1999. Since the program's inception, the County has experienced many successes and challenges in those 27 years. Successes include the acquisition of numerous public artworks that are on public display throughout the County, including on City of Fort Pierce-owned or controlled properties.
In May 2024, the County contracted with a consultant to conduct a condition assessment and an inventory of the County's public art collection. The results of the condition assessment and the inventory identified 32 public artworks. The report included an assessment of each artwork's condition, repair and restoration needs, location, artist and approximate valuation. The inventory revealed that 10 of the artworks were located on City of Fort Pierce-owned or controlled properties and of these 10 artworks, 8 of them are needing repair and restoration.
On October 27, 2024, the County issued an Art Conservator Services RFP that was publicly advertised and posted on Demand Star and also directly emailed to potential firms. On November 20, 2024, the Art Conservator Services proposals were due to the County, but no proposals were received. On January 19, 2025, the Art Conservator Services RFP was re-advertised and also directly emailed to potential firms. On February 19, 2025, two proposals were received. On June 13, 2025, the selection committee evaluated and ranked the proposals that were received and the highest ranking firm was selected by the evaluation committee.
On July 1, 2025, RLA Conservation, LLC, was awarded the contract to perform Art Conservator Services for St. Lucie County. No services have been rendered yet.
The City of Fort Pierce has agreed to cooperate in sharing the cost for the repair and refurbishments of the public art pieces that are located on City-owned or controlled property. The total cost to repair and restore the 8 public artworks is $72,875. Fifty-percent (50%) of this cost, $36,437.50, will be paid by the City of Fort Pierce. Once all repairs and refurbishments are completed, the County will transfer ownership of the 10 public art pieces on City-owned or controlled property from the County to the City. After the transfer of ownership, the City of Fort Pierce will be responsible for all repair, maintenance and restoration moving forward.
City staff have indicated this Interlocal Agreement will be presented to the Fort Pierce City Commission on February 17th.
This request is in alignment with Strategic initiatives TC 5.1.2, TC 5.2.1 and TC 5.2.4.

description:
Stormwater culverts direct and channel the flow of stormwater under driveways, roads, sidewalks and other obstructions and are an integral component of stormwater management. Culverts fail over time due to maintenance, environmental or installation issues. Culvert failure can lead to localized flooding which may impede safe conditions of ingress and egress for owners and residents of property in the affected area as well as the traveling public, visitors, emergency responders and other public service providers. Some culvert owners may lack the resources to pay for improvements and repairs.
In 2021, the Board established a voluntary program, Ordinance No. 21-004, to which eligible property owners can apply for and receive funding to improve or repair culverts and then repay this funding through the imposition of a non-ad valorem special assessment against the improved property collected in annual installments on the tax roll.
The attached Resolution No. 2026-19 is the Assessment Resolution as required by County's Ordinance No. 21-004, as amended. The purpose of this resolution relates to the imposition and collection of special assessments to fund stormwater culvert improvements within the Culvert 2026-02 MSBU, determine that real property therein will be specially benefitted, establish the method of assessing the cost of the improvements, approve the assessment roll, and provide an effective date.

description:
The County Administrator has discussed with the Board the need for a proposed extension to the existing 0.5 percent infrastructure surtax. Proceeds from the surtax, if approved, would be used to improve public roads, reduce traffic congestion, reduce neighborhood flooding, improve local water quality and other similar uses. Implementation of the proposed surtax requires that the Board adopt an ordinance that directs the Supervisor of Elections to schedule a referendum election to allow the qualified electors of the County to vote on the levy of the proposed surtax. It is anticipated that the Cities and the Village will adopt resolutions requesting that the Board adopt an ordinance for a period of ten (10) years. In this regard, attached is a draft ordinance that, if adopted, would direct the Supervisor of Elections to hold a referendum election on November 3, 2026 on the ballot question set out in the draft ordinance. If approved by the voters on November 3, 2026, the proposed surtax would be effective for ten (10) years beginning January 1, 2029. The proceeds would be distributed to the County and municipalities pursuant to the formula set out in Section 218.62, Florida Statutes.
Attached are two draft versions of the ordinance: Draft Ordinance No. 26-XXXA and Draft Ordinance No. 26-XXXB for the Board to determine which draft ordinance will move forward and grant permission for a public hearing.

description:
Schmidt Nichols submitted a petition, on behalf of Almeria Developers, LLC, for a Final Major Site Plan to be known as the Almeria Residential Development for a +/-12.88 acre parcel. The Smallwood Ave. property is in the White City area, east of the South US 1 corridor, approximately 1/3 mile south of Midway Rd.
The proposed Almeria Residential multi-family development would consist of 64 detached condominium units, a type of development sometimes referred to as "horizontal multi-family." No platting is proposed with units sold through a Declaration of Condominium, and each owner owning only the building and being responsible for their share of common area upkeep costs. Units could be sold or rented.
The subject property is zoned RM-5 (Residential Multi-Family-5 units per acre), with a Future Land Use designation of RM (Residential Medium, up to 9 units per acre). The subject properties lie within the Urban Service Boundary (USB). Project density is proposed at 4.97 units per acre, under the maximum 5 units per acre of the RM-5 zoning district.
The subject property contains isolated wetlands and a high density of native pine, oak and palm trees, many of which would be impacted by the proposed design which carries a substantial mitigation requirement for the project. The County Environmental Resources Department (ERD) approved a wetland waiver, and the development has also received permits from FPUA, the Florida Department of Environmental Protection, the N. St. Lucie River Water Control District, and the South Florida Water Management District.
The project was designated as a Major Site Plan in accordance with Land Development Code Section 11.02.02. C. 7. as the Planning and Development Services Director determined the proposed development should be more thoroughly considered and reviewed because of its location or potential for impact on public facilities, natural resources, and public safety.

description:
Tornadoes from Hurricane Milton in October 2024 caused significant damage to vegetation, structures, and various critical infrastructure in the northern and eastern parts of Lakewood Park. Eastwood Canal parallels Eastwood Drive and serves as a primary drainage canal for the central and eastern Lakewood Park community. The canal suffered significant damage from a tornado, including uprooted and fallen trees, accumulation of windblown debris, and several localized erosion washouts.
The diminished stormwater conveyance capacity of the Eastwood Canal posed a threat to the health, welfare, and safety of the residents within Lakewood Park. St. Lucie County sought Federal grant funding assistance for the recovery effort and successfully acquired an Emergency Watershed Protection (EWP) Program grant from the United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Natural Resource Conservation Service (NRCS) in the amount of $223,296.70.
The Eastwood Canal Restoration Project removed fallen trees and storm debris within and along the approximate 2.2 miles of canal. The project also included several repairs to the drainage outfalls and improvements to the canal bank slopes, resulting in more resilient infrastructure for the County’s critical stormwater management system.
In order to expedite the repairs and best utilize County resources, the Public Works Department's Engineering Division designed the plans for the repair project in-house. All the survey work, estimation, drafting, engineering design and specification and inspection was performed without the need for competitive bidding, accelerating the project several months and saving tens of thousands of dollars versus privatizing the effort. Staff will provide a brief presentation on benefits achieved by the approach to the project.
The project was advertised on July 20th, 2025, and the bids were opened on August 8th, 2025. Three (3) bids were received, and the lowest responsible bidder was Environmental Land Development (ELD).
The construction budget was:
Base Bid: $153,100.00
10% Contingency: $ 15,310.00
Total Construction Budget $168,410.00
The total amount spent on the construction was $165,528.65, which included some of the contingency for additional approved work. Therefore, the project was completed under budget with a remaining amount of $2,881.35.
Staff monitored the construction and determined the project was completed in substantial conformance with the plans and specifications.

FDOT Central Office is preparing a grant application for the FRA Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail (FSP) Grant Program. The application establishes FDOT's Statewide Advancement of Feature Enhancements at Intercity Passenger Rail Crossings (SAFE-IPR) Program.
The SAFE-IPR Program is a statewide, programmatic approach to implementing safety countermeasures at 910 intercity passenger rail crossings. The Program reflects a comprehensive and coordinated strategy for addressing safety risks that affect communities across Florida. Proposed improvements, including upgraded traffic control devices, enhanced pedestrian treatments, improved lighting, and revised approach geometries, will help reduce safety risks at crossings while improving the movement of people and goods, emergency response operations, and quality of life for residents, visitors, and businesses.
FDOT District 4 is requesting assistance in obtaining support letters for this Federal grant application. The improvements will improve the safety of pedestrian and motor vehicle users as they approach at-grade railway crossings in St. Lucie County. As this application is time-sensitive, the Chair has signed the attached letter and this item seeks ratification by the Board as an after-the-fact action.

description:
On September 5, 1995, Central Florida Foreign-Trade Zone, Inc. applied for a Foreign Trade Zone (FTZ) encompassing St. Lucie, Indian River, and Okeechobee County’s. The application was approved by the FTZ Board in Washington D.C. (October 24, 1996) and FTZ Zone 218 was created (Board Order 851). Subsequently, the supervision of FTZ Zone 218 went through some management re-configurations until it was ultimately transferred to St. Lucie County in 2021 (the current “Grantee”). Upon transfer, a subsequent Alternative Site Framework (ASF) Application was filed by St. Lucie County to take advantage of a more streamlined approval process for subzone designations within the broader FTZ Zone 218. That ASF application was approved on February 22, 2022, and provided St. Lucie County with a more efficient way to endorse and establish future FTZ subzones for specific companies/industries within the tri-county area.
A formal ASF subzone designation request for Oculus Surgical, Inc. was recently submitted by county staff on December 17, 2025. The proposed subzone area encompasses an 8.18-acre warehouse facility at 9850 SW Discovery Way, Port St. Lucie (St. Lucie County). The zone site operator (Oculus Surgical, Inc.) proposes to produce, warehouse and distribute surgical and eye diagnostic equipment for Opthamology. The attached Operations Agreement is specific to our recent request and outlines all responsibilities between the County (as the Grantee) and Oculus Surgical, Inc. (the “Zone Site Operator”).
ASF subzone 218C will ultimately provide Oculus Surgical, Inc. with a new suite of options to attract and retain business within St. Lucie County, and a site walk-through with Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is currently being scheduled.
All Site Zone Operators under the ASF shall establish standards of operation and management set out in a site-specific Foreign-Trade Zone Operations Manual which conforms to all requirements of the FTZ Board and Customs. The County is in no way required to or obligated to monitor day-to-day activities of any subzones approved under the ASF framework.

description:
The Transit Department is requesting a sole source procurement for purchase, and implementation of a software upgrade for the fixed route system from the current software program - RouteMatch to TripSpark's Streets software with the addition of automatic passenger counters on all fixed route buses. The existing transit software was purchased from RouteMatch in 2020. Since that time, Routematch was acquired by TripSpark. As a result, support and updates for the RouteMatch platform will be phased out, and the company is focusing efforts on transitioning existing customers to TripSpark. The current licenses that were previously purchased through RouteMatch will be honored, which will equate to a large savings off the TripSpark Streets system. TripSpark can also align a smooth transition plan from the current platform to the new platform. In addition to this, Transit migrated from RouteMatch to TripSpark's NovusDR software for the paratransit and microtransit in 2025. Using the same software for all three services will help to make the transit system more efficient and will make trip planning easier for transit riders. A draft of the amendment to our existing Software License and Maintenance Agreement incorporating the software upgrade is attached.
The transit software platform is critical to the daily functions of the transit system. The upgrade of this system will ensure critical service provision, good customer service, and increased efficiencies in the operation of the fixed route service. The cost of this upgrade will be $750,055. This sole-source purchase is the most cost-effective way to upgrade the existing system. The Transit Department recently received a grant from the Federal Transit Administration for this software upgrade. The grant will cover 100% of the cost.
This project is in accordance with the Strategic Plan Policy PT 1.4.3.

description:
In 2024, Ashley Capital, LLC and St. Lucie County entered a contract (Option Agreement) for the County to convey to Ashley Capital, LLC +/-99.77 acres located on Kings Highway. In May 2025, Ashley Capital purchased 60 adjacent acres from the St. Lucie County School Board thereby creating the +/-159.77-acre subject site. The Option Agreement with the County requires Ashley Capital to obtain an amendment of the Future Land Use Map to MXD (Mixed Use Development) (or another appropriate future land use designation) and obtain an amendment of the Official Zoning Atlas to place the land in the PNRD (Planned Non-Residential Development) Zoning District accompanied by the PNRD Preliminary Development Plan. Subsequent to accomplishing these steps, Ashley Capital may exercise its option to purchase the land from the County.
The Option Agreement requires St. Lucie County to accomplish certain steps regarding the Research and Education Park Overlay Zone, a lease with the Treasure Coast Education and Research Development Authority (TCERDA) and certain restrictive covenants, which it has completed.
This public hearing is regarding the proposed change of the RS (Residential Suburban) category for +/-127.41 acres and the SD (Special District) category for +/-32.36 acres to MXD (Mixed Use Development) with sub-area policies to permit development of +/-1.6 million square feet of light industrial space. This is the Transmittal Public Hearing at which the Board must determine whether to transmit the proposed Future Land Use Map Amendment to the state and regional reviewing agencies. If the Board determines to transmit the proposed amendment, it will return to the Board for consideration of adoption at a second Public Hearing. The request to rezone to PNRD with the proposed Preliminary Development Plan providing for some 13 buildings ranging from 50,000 sq. ft. to 200,000 sq. ft.will also be scheduled for a future, separate public hearing.

description:
Resolution No. 2026-21- Consenting to the Membership Interest Purchase and Sale Agreement and the Resulting Change of Control of Fort Pierce FBO, LLC (APP). APP has requested the County's consent Membership Interest Purchase and Sale Agreement of 100% of the equity interests held by RW Pegasus Holdings LLC (a subsidiary of Ridgewood Infrastructure) in RW Pegasus IntermediateCo, LLC to BC Flex Midco, LLC, an affiliate of Bain Capital Real Estate and the Resulting Change of Control of Fort Pierce FBO, LLC (APP).
The County was notified by APP in late January of the agreement to purchase 100% of the equity interests of APP by Bain Capital. Dan Harrow, Chief Executive Officer of APP, requested approval of the proposed acquisition. Mr. Harrow indicated the "Membership Interest Purchase and Sale Agreement was signed on January 22, 2026. Subject to obtaining the necessary airport approvals, the parties are aiming to consummate the Sale by the end of February, or early March the latest.”
Ridgewood Infrastructure, LLC, (RW Pegasus Holdings, LLC) with ownership interest in APP Properties, Inc. and APP Properties, LLC, which conduct the APP Jet Centers business (APP) requires the County’s consent to sell to Bain Capital.
APP Properties, Inc. (APP) is the owner and operator of Fort Pierce FBO, LLC, dba APP Jet Center Fort Pierce, the ground lessee at the Treasure Coast International Airport.
The current lease agreements (identified below) with Fort Pierce FBO, LLC, require County consent to any assignment of interest or transfer of control of the lessee.
First Amendment to the Second Amended and Restated Lease Agreement between St. Lucie County and Fort Pierce FBO, LLC dba APP Jet Center (successor in interest to Air Charter of Florida, Inc.), dated November 4, 2025.
Third Amendment to the October 10, 2000 Amended and Restated Lease Agreement between St. Lucie County and Fort Pierce FBO, LLC dba APP Jet Center (successor in interest to B& E Houck Enterprises, Inc.), dated July 11, 2023.
-----------------------
2026 Proposed Sale:
Bain Capital Real Estate was created in 2010, has joined Bain Capital in 2018. Bain Capital Real Estate is in the process of establishing a leading general aviation platform including FBOs and aviation infrastructure assets across the US. Bain Capital Real Estate’s plans concerning APP is to invest capital to enhance existing hangars, develop additional hangers and improve FBO infrastructure across the APP business, including at St. Lucie County.
The Bain Capital Real Estate website (https://www.baincapitalrealestate.com/) states, as of June 30, 2025, they have $10.7B equity invested across ~700 assets, and a ~$18M average equity investment, and 100+ dedicated professionals to leverage experience and expertise.
Information submitted by Chris Leddy, Managing Director of Bain Capital Real Estate, states, “[W]e are partnering with Mark Johnstone (former Signature Aviation CEO – Signature is the largest FBO network in the US) who will lead APP post transaction. Specific to aviation, Bain Capital has invested over $4.5 billion across a number of investments including Virgin Australia, arajet, Icelandair, Wheels Up, MRO Holdings, Griffin Global AM, Tenax Aerospace, Jetstream Aviation Capital, Titan, ITP Aero, KP Aviation and others.”
The resulting company will still do business as APP Jet Center Fort Pierce; however, the Board will consist primarily of representatives from Bain Capital Real Estate, who will control the Company. Benefits of the merger include the availability of additional capital to complete existing APP projects and the development of new projects with the County as a partner.
-----------------------
2021 Prior Sale:
On December 7, 2021, the Board consented merger of APP Properties, Inc. into an Affiliate of Ridgewood Infrastructure, LLC and the resulting change of control of Fort Pierce FBO, LLC., as set forth in Resolution No. 21-428.
Ridgewood Infrastructure, LLC ("Ridgewood"), a New York-based investment fund with more than $6 billion under management, proposed to acquire the APP Properties. The resulting company continued doing business as APP Jet Center Fort Pierce; however, the Board consisted primarily of representatives from Ridgewood, who controlled the Company. Benefits of the merger include the availability of additional capital to complete existing APP projects.
The Board determined that consent to the merger and change of control of Fort Pierce FBO, LLC, was in the best interest of the County as the merger would increase the availability of capital to complete existing projects and the opportunity to develop new projects with the County as a partner.
The Board consented to the merger, via Resolution 21-428, which included a Cure of Designated Deficiencies as follows:
APP, Ridgewood and RW acknowledge the receipt of notice of certain deficiencies under the Leases,
APP agrees to take the actions set forth in Section A of the " Action Plan" attached as Exhibit " A" hereto and incorporated herein by reference, and
APP, Ridgewood and RW further acknowledge that the failure to take the actions set forth in Section A of the Action Plan shall be deemed a default under the applicable Lease.”

description:
Through an lnterlocal Agreement with the Sheriff, the County manages inmate medical services at the jail. On May 7, 2024 the Board approved NaphCare as the preferred inmate medical vendor and a contract with NaphCare became effective on July 29, 2024.
Historically, the inmate medical services contract has included a Substance Abuse Counselor position that provides substance abuse counseling to qualified inmates at the jail as part of the Journey Forward Program run by the Public Defender's office. When the inmate medical services contract was transferred from the Sheriff to the County, the County continued to include Journey Forward's Substance Abuse Counselor position in its inmate medical services contract with NaphCare to ensure continuity and avoid a lapse in services. Now that some time has passed, and NaphCare has been successfully managing the contract, staff recommends Journey Forward's Substance Abuse Counselor position be placed where it most properly belongs, under the Public Defender's office.
Staff is therefore seeking approval to remove the Substance Abuse Counselor position from the required staffing in the NaphCare contract and temporarily move that position to the County via contract until the Public Defender can add the position to the Journey Forward program at the start of the State's fiscal year on July 1st. The funds removed from the NaphCare contract for eliminating the Substance Abuse Counselor position will be used by the County to pay for that position until June 30, 2026. As of July 1st the remaining funds will be transferred to the Journey Forward program to add the Substance Abuse Counselor position. The funding of the Substance Abuse Counselor position is not changing, merely the mechanism by which the position is funded. Going forward, the position will be funded directly as part of the County's grant to the Journey Forward program.
NaphCare will remove the Substance Abuse Counselor position from the contract effective February 1, 2026, and permanently reduce their Year 2 Base Annual Price. The pro-rated Year 2 reduction will be used by the County to add the Substance Abuse Counselor for the months of February 1, 2026, through June 30, 2026. Beginning July 1, 2026, the County will increase its contribution to the Journey Forward program by $90,237.90 per year.
A draft of the proposed 1st amendment to the NaphCare contract is attached as well as a draft consultant agreement.

description:
The St. Lucie County Regional Resilience Plan (RRP) and Resilience Vulnerability Assessment – Other Hazards (RVA-OH) were presented to the Board of County Commissioners at the December 9, 2025 Informal Meeting. In addition, the Draft RRP and RVA-OH were presented to the City of Port St. Lucie, City of Fort Pierce and Town of St. Lucie Village in December 2025.
The attached Final Regional Resilience Plan (RRP) corrects minor typographical and formatting errors, as well as specific modifications to:Front Cover: changed from ‘Draft’ to ‘Final’ and date updated to January 2026
Section 10.0: updates to Benefit-Cost Analysis summary paragraph
Appendix F: added Benefit-Cost Analysis on Select SLC Conservation Sites
The attached Final Resilience Vulnerability Assessment (RVA) report corrects minor typographical and formatting errors, as well as specific modifications to:
Front Cover: changed from ‘Draft’ to ‘Final’ and date updated to January 2026
Section 2.3: minor changes and updated numbers to stakeholder engagement paragraph
As background, in 2022, St. Lucie County was awarded a CDBG-Mitigation grant in the amount of $600,000 and entered into an agreement with the Florida Department of Commerce (Commerce) to develop a community-wide St. Lucie County Regional Resilience Plan. The initiative included conducting an in-depth Resilience Vulnerability Assessment (RVA) looking at various hazards to identify local risks and inform potential mitigation and adaptation strategy recommendations as part of the RRP.
The planning process included extensive community engagement and regular meetings of the St. Lucie Resilience Steering Committee, which played a vital role in shaping the RRP and RVA. The Steering Committee represented various St. Lucie County, Port St. Lucie, Fort Pierce and St. Lucie Village departments, as well as other local and regional agencies.
The Regional Resilience Plan represents the first step in developing a comprehensive and collaborative approach to adapt to and mitigate the effects of extreme and disruptive natural events. Acceptance of the RRP and RVA positions the county and municipalities to be eligible for state and federal grant funding to support resilience initiatives. Acceptance of the RRP does not constitute adoption of specific policies or actions recommended in the plan, but rather an agreement to consider recommendations as another tool for future planning and decision-making toward creating a sustainable and resilient community.
This project furthers St. Lucie County strategic objectives, including: EP 4.1.1 – Implement and continue to update the St. Lucie Regional Resilience Plan that addresses natural resources, the built environment, and citizen safety and well-being; and QI 3.3.4 – Actively seek resilience and funding opportunities to increase sustainability of infrastructure and facilities.

description:
In 2024, the County issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 24-055, Develop Aero West Parcels at Treasure Coast International Airport. Aero West consisted of six parcels totaling approximately 13 acres. The intent for this RFP was for qualified applicants to submit proposals to develop and operate aeronautical facilities on one or more undeveloped parcels of land on Aero West.
On July 17, 2024, responses to RFP No. 24-055, included a sole proposal in response to RFP No. 24-055. Aircraft Turbine Works for Parcel A (686 companies were notified, and 53 RFP documents were distributed). Aircraft Turbine Works proposal included a phased approach, beginning with the construction of one 12,000 square foot hangar and 3,600 square feet of office space on approximately 2 acres on Parcel A.
On August 8, 2024, the selection committee evaluated the proposal from Aircraft Turbine Works and determined that the proposal was responsive and made a recommendation to move forward with negotiations. On August 27, 2024, the Board approved the selection committee recommendation for RFP No. 24-055 and permission to conduct contract negotiations with Aircraft Turbine Works; and if negotiations were successful, award the contract to Aircraft Turbine Works. County staffed engaged with Aircraft Turbine Works to negotiate a lease. Through the negotiations, Aircraft Turbine Works requested to add Parcel B to their proposal and build a second hangar and office. In June of 2025, the County entered into a lease agreement with Aircraft Turbine Works (Finnish Strong LLC).
During the negotiations with Aircraft Turbine Works, their representatives stated that another tenant at the airport, Treasure Coast Jet Center, was interested in leasing land at Aero West. In June of 2025, Treasure Coast Jet Center submitted a letter of interest in leasing Parcel C of Aero West to develop a maintenance hangar and office. Section 125.35, F. S., and the St. Lucie County International Airport Leasing Policy dated December 12, 2006, provide for leasing property on the Airport for aviation purposes (as an "airport facility") as a first priority and that Airport property identified for aviation uses may be leased without seeking competitive proposals.
Through the RFP there were no other proposals or indicated interest in the other parcels of Aero West or during the subsequent negotiation discussions with Aircraft Turbine Works. The new proposal from Treasure Coast Jet Center did not impede and was reasonably compatible with the Aircraft Turbine Works proposal. County staffed engaged with Treasure Coast Jet Center to negotiate a lease. Through the negotiations, Treasure Coast Jet Center requested to add Parcel D to their proposal and build a second hangar and office.
The proposed lease is in alignment with Strategic Plan Objectives ECON 2.4.3 and ECON 2.1.1.

description:
The “Work Camper” program was established for St. Lucie County Environmentally Significant Lands (ESL’s)program in 2002. This program provides a volunteer with a space and utility hook up for their own recreational vehicle for use as a temporary residence in exchange for a minimum of twenty (20) hours of service each week. Each Work Camper puts in a minimum of 1,040 hours of work annually, benefitting the County the equivalent of $28,288.00 of labor each year (based on 2020 Independent Sector’s Value of Volunteer Time =$27.20/ hour).
The work camper for the Petravice Family Preserve will be responsible for tasks specified in the attached contract, including opening and closing gates, helping to maintain parking lot and nature trails in neat and clean condition, patrolling sites/site security, and some mowing and exotic plant removal. The St. Lucie County Environmental Resources Department manages over 11,000 acres of public preserves owned by the St. Lucie County Board of Commissioners. The Petravice Family Preserve is a 24.77-acre public preserve purchased on May 28, 2014, with funds from the voter-approved Environmentally Significant Lands Bond Program. The property is located along the St. Lucie River, within the planned North Fork corridor and is perfectly situated to establish a “hub” for both the Greenways & Trails (GW&T) & Paddling Trails programs. A canoe/kayak launch allows paddlers access to a stretch of the creek that does not see high volumes of boat traffic, making it ideal for quiet and peaceful exploration and appreciation of nature. The Work Camper program is one of several mutually beneficial partnerships being established on the Petravice Family Preserveto help satisfy shared needs and achieve common goals.

The purpose of this Request for Qualifications is to award to the most highly qualified Construction Manager at Risk (“CMAR”) firm or entity to act as the CMAR for the new renovation of 8881 S. US Highway 1 for Tax Collector and County Services.
The anticipated work for this CMAR contract will be decided into two phases:
Phase I – Preconstruction Services: The Preconstruction Services phase will include design and constructability reviews, any necessary value-engineering, cost estimating, scheduling, building condition assessment, and other preconstruction activities. Phase II – Construction Services: The Construction Services phase will include continued design reviews of final Construction Documents, procurement of subcontractors and vendors, self-performance of certain construction elements as agreed, and full execution of the construction work in accordance with the GMP and approved schedule.

description:
Contract C23-07-807 was executed by Infrastructure Management Services on October 23, 2023. The negotiated scope of services provided a Pavement Condition Index (PCI) and Pavement Management Report to evaluate and develop cost-effective budget estimates using different pavement rehabilitation strategies for all County maintained arterial and collector roads. In addition, data was collected on County maintained assets, including curbs, curb ramps, crosswalks, medians, swales, catch basins, manholes and guardrails. The overall intent of the infrastructure inventory and condition assessment was to provide the County with a systematic, consistent, and reproducible method of determining priorities and optimal time of maintenance to economically manage the County's roadway system within an established budget. Due to funding limitations, local neighborhood road data was not collected. The County maintains 215 miles of local paved roads and analyzing conditions to assign the right strategy and proper timing is critical to maximize cost-effectiveness of the local road repaving program.
The attached proposal is to perform an infrastructure inventory and condition assessment and develop a pavement management plan for all County maintained paved local roads. Additionally, the condition of all County maintained sidewalks and signs will be assessed for paved local roads, as well as arterial and collector roads. The data collected will be compatible with the County’s Geographic Information System (GIS), and have the ability to generate reports for budgeting, presentations, and be utilized with future work order systems.

description:
St. Lucie County has helped re-establish a Local Arts Agency (LAA) and has worked with the St. Lucie Cultural Alliance (SLCA) the last five (5) years to continue to develop and support an effective arts and culture segment that improves the quality of life among residents, and also brings a positive economic impact by attracting cultural tourists to the County.
The SLCA, acting in the capacity of the County’s Local Arts Agency (LAA), is requesting funding support from the Tourist Development Council. On Wednesday, December 10, 2025, the Tourist Development Council unanimously supported funding the St. Lucie Cultural Alliance in the amount of $150,000 for one year. As proposed, the St. Lucie Cultural Alliance shall use the funds solely to plan, promote, and execute cultural programs, events, and activities designed to increase tourism and enhance the cultural visibility of the region (“Tourism-Enhancing Activities”).
The agreement with the SLCA shall include the following activities in the scope of work:Maintain a functioning and effective Board of Directors
Oversee and implement all consulting, financial, website, support, social media, marketing, and reporting activities by SLCA staff or contracted services
Provide a nexus for partnerships that support the mission
Ensure timely, detailed, bi-annual reporting of SLCA activities to the Tourist Development Council, St. Lucie County Administration and the Board of County Commissioners. This reporting shall include the financial standing of the SLCA, other funds raised and details of how all funds are being spent
Continue implementing the coherent branded cultural offerings
Market St. Lucie’s cultural venues, artists, assets, and events with the goal of increasing attendance and visitors from out-of-the-area at St. Lucie County’s cultural programs
Work towards a strategy that builds and creates a self-sustaining LAA and advances the arts and culture sector
Funding
A proposed 1-year contract agreement, from January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026, outlines the funding support provided by the Tourist Development Council. Beginning on January 1, 2026, which may conclude on June 30, 2026, the agreement provides funding in the amount of seventy-five thousand and 00/100 Dollars ($75,000.00) to be provided in two installments of $37,500.00. On or before June 30, 2026, and upon an approved evaluation by the Tourist Development Council and the Board of County Commissioners, continued funding support will conclude on December 31, 2026, and will be an additional seventy-five thousand and 00/100 Dollars ($75,000.00) which will be provided two installments of $37,500. The total amount of the twelve (12) month agreement is not to exceed one hundred fifty thousand and 00/100 Dollars ($150,000.00).
Reporting
For the Tourist Development and Board of County Commissioners evaluation, four reports shall be received from the SLCA. The first report shall be received on or before March 31, 2026.
The second report on or before June 30, 2026.
The third report shall be received on or before September 30, 2026.
The fourth report on or before December 31, 2026.
The evaluation of the first and second reports will be a determining factor by the Tourist Development Council and the Board of County Commissioners to continue payments under the agreement for the second six months, or from July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 of the agreement. The Tourist Development Council and/or the Board of County Commissioners may request that the SLCA present their report at a TDC or BOCC meeting.
Performance Reports
Each performance report must include information and supporting documentation and/or data that shows proof of performance to increase tourism and enhance the cultural visibility of the County:Narrative summary of activities;
Report on matching funds - documented proof of 100% of matching funds are required. Each report shall document the performance and efforts to raise and/or secure matching funds (local, state and regional grants, donations, in-kind donations with supporting documentation, sponsorships, membership dues, income for services rendered by the SLCA (i.e. curating exhibitions, rotating art, etc.) and funding partnerships shall qualify as matching funds);
Complete attendance and tourism metrics at hosted events;
Financial accountability documentation - Documentation shall indicate how the County funds were spent, and detail the results of the SLCA's efforts during the preceding period;
Summary of marketing reach and partnerships;
Copies of marketing materials and analytics.
Evaluation of outcomes and recommendations for future planning and/or programming
Evaluation
The Tourist Development Council and the Board of County Commissioners shall assess each Performance Report to determine compliance with the milestone benchmarks. Failure to meet, or make reasonable progress toward, these benchmarks may result in:Delay or withholding of milestone payments;
Requirement to submit corrective action plans;
Reduction in future funding;
Requirement to return funds to the County;
Termination of the Agreement, as permitted by law.
This item is proposed in accordance with Strategic Plan provision TC 5.2.1 and TC 5.2.2.

description:
This agreement between the FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION (FDOT) and St. Lucie County (County) authorizes the parties to enter into an agreement for certain roadway corridors to be taken off the State Highway System and certain roadway corridors to be placed onto the State Highway System. The County and FDOT have requested the transfer of:
SR-607/Emerson Avenue from SR-614/Indrio Road to Indian River County Line OFF the State Highway System
SR-615/N. 25th Street from CR-611B/Edwards Road to US-1/SR-5/Federal Highway OFF the State Highway System
CR-712/Midway Road from I-95 to US-1/SR-5/Federal Highway ON to the State Highway System
CR-614/Indrio Road from SR-713/Kings Highway to US-1/SR-5/Federal Highway ON to the State Highway System
These roadway locations are graphically depicted on the location map, attached here as Exhibit A-1. Roadways have been considered for addition onto the State system based on the function and category of these roadways including, but not limited to, connection to the Strategic Intermodal System (SIS) corridors and facilities, evacuation routes, and location of critical facilities. Both Indrio Road and Midway Road connect to major roadways including US-1 and I-95. Conversely, roadway corridors that lack these certain qualifiers are requested to be transferred from FDOT to the County for perpetual ownership and maintenance.
The agreement will transfer jurisdictional ownership and maintenance of all roadway elements, including roadbed, signage and marking, sidewalks, curbing, guardrails, bicycle paths, traffic control devices, drainage infrastructure, bridges and drainage ponds. For transfers OFF the state system, the transfer will occur upon the satisfactory completion of work program projects along these roadways. North 25th Street was recently resurfaced by FDOT and construction is completed. Emerson Avenue has a resurfacing project currently underway. Upon closeout of both of these projects, expected by mid-2026, the roadways will be transferred to the County.
For transfers ON the state system:
Indrio Road will transfer upon final execution of this agreement by all parties.
Midway Road will transfer between Jenkins Road and US-1 upon final execution of this agreement by all parties. The section of Midway Road between I-95 and Jenkins Road will remain County responsibility until the notice to proceed is issued for the 4-lane road widening project between Glades Cut Off Road and Jenkins Road, including the southbound turnpike ramps, expected to occur in mid-2027.
It is common policy for FDOT to subordinate maintenance and expense of non-standard or beautification items to local jurisdictions using maintenance agreements. The County will continue to maintain the enhanced median landscaping and provide right of way mowing along Midway Road, as these are non-standard enhancements along the corridor. Enhanced landscaping and/or street lighting along N. 25th Street, generally beginning north of SR-70/Virginia Avenue are currently maintained by the City of Fort Pierce under highway maintenance agreements that automatically transfer with the transfer of road ownership. It is the County's intention to continue to obligate the City to maintain these improvements at the City's expense in accordance with the existing agreements.
Portions of Midway Road were widened to 4-lanes using Federal funds, which requires the County to enter into a maintenance agreement with FDOT in order to remain compliant with federal regulations. This agenda item contains a resolution to enter into this agreement, attached as Exhibit C-1.
The existing FEC rail crossing along Midway Road located just to the east of Glades Cut Off Road will remain the responsibility of the County based on the terms of the current license agreement between the County and FEC, until such time as FDOT and FEC negotiate and sign a new agreement.

description:
St. Lucie County has filed suit against various companies, including the Distributors and Settling Defendants, in what has been referred to as the "National Prescription Opiate Litigation".
On January 5, 2026, the County Attorney was contacted by Eric Romano, an attorney from the firm representing the County in litigation, to provide an update on a proposed settlement from Publix. After further discussion and consideration, Mr. Romano emailed the County Attorney with the recommendation that St. Lucie County settle its claim against Publix, citing several factors including costs associated with potential litigation in the future and the likelihood of success on pending motions.
Publix has offered $375,000 collectively to settle the claims of St. Lucie, St. Johns, and Marion counties. It has not offered a specific amount solely to settle St. Lucie County's claim, and there have been no agreements or proposals as to how any such settlement funds would be allocated between the three counties, assuming all agree to settle (although the letter from Publix's counsel provides a rough estimate of what they believe to be the value of each case). ​

description:
As part of St. Lucie County's commitment to a resilient future, and consistent with the County's strategic plan, presented for acceptance is the update to the Stormwater Master Plan (SMP), which has been underway for two years and fully funded using proceeds from the American Rescue Plan.
The previous version of the County's stormwater plan was completed in 1992 and although it is relevant, the outputs and assumptions are no longer as useful due to the changes in future land use and growth patterns the area has experienced since that time. Furthermore, the tools to model current and future scenarios have evolved. This update uses the latest in hydrologic and hydraulic (H&H) modeling to look beyond today's conditions and plan effectively for the next 20-year cycle of growth, taking into account future scenarios including higher sea level and riverine elevations, more intense storms and a built-out environment. The modeling predicts the impact of flood waters on critical roads and infrastructure and prescribes opportunities in the form of conceptual projects that could aid in reducing the extent and duration of flooding within the study area. Key deliverables include a digital model of the identified priority basins, the stormwater report including the assumptions and findings, and a 20-year capital implementation program with conceptual project costs.
A crucial element of the plan is public participation and this effort has been achieved by a multi-faceted approach along the development cycle of the Stormwater Master Plan update that involved stakeholder interviews, coordination with local flood control agencies and a robust set of 9 separate in-person and virtual public workshops that helped staff receive feedback on problem areas and related stormwater and water quality concerns.
The original project budget was $2,295,740. While a final invoice has not yet been received, the project is anticipated to come in significantly under budget. As of Nov 25, 2025, $1,573,655.97 of the total amount has been expended.
Public Works staff has been aided by a consultant team led by Tetra Tech, Inc. and this presentation represents the culmination of work completed and the final results of the Stormwater Master Plan.

description:
Since 2005/2006, the Board has funded New Horizons of the Treasure Coast Inc. to provide services to individuals involved with the criminal justice system that suffer from mental and/or substance abuse disorders. The $533,050.00 in funding from the Fine and Forfeiture Fund provides housing, medication, case management, psycho-social rehabilitation, and substance abuse services in community-based settings. The contract for services is for $533,050.00.
Early intervention opportunities for mental health and substance abuse offenders provide these defendants/offenders with access to alternative more appropriate community mental health treatment at a cost significantly less than the cost of incarceration.
New Horizons of the Treasure Coast, Inc. partners closely with the courts and criminal justice system to provide a broad range of mental health and substance abuse services. As a non-profit corporation providing residential and outpatient mental health and substance abuse rehabilitation for over 50 years, it has been the primary local provider of substance abuse and mental health services.
There are currently 193 active cases. The national average cost of mental health cases in custody is $125.00 per day. Mental health cases can stay up to seven (7) times longer than the average inmate (the average is 35 days). It should also be noted that the recidivism rate is only 9% for individuals completing the mental health court program. The national average for mental health clients is 78% recidivism.

description:
In 2007, St. Lucie County provided a Two Million Dollar ($2,000,000) Hurricane Housing Recovery Program loan to Madison Cay, Ltd. to support the development of the 132-unit affordable housing complex known as Madison Cay Apartments. The loan is evidenced by a Secured Promissory Note, Mortgage, Assignment of Rents and Security Agreement, Land Use Restriction Agreement, and related loan documents.
As part of a property acquisition and resyndication transaction, Lincoln Avenue Communities is acquiring Madison Cay Apartments through its affiliate, Madison Cay Preservation, Ltd. The transaction includes new tax-exempt bond financing administered by the Housing Finance Authority of St. Lucie County, with the senior loan to be purchased by Freddie Mac. In connection with the ownership transfer and financing structure, staff has reviewed the limited County actions required to allow the transaction to proceed while preserving the County’s existing loan position and long-term affordability requirements.
Staff are presenting the following documents for Board consideration and approval:
An Assumption and Global Modification of Mortgage, Assignment of Rents and Security Agreement, Secured Promissory Note, Land Use Restriction Agreement, and Other Loan Documents, which provides for the assumption of the County loan by the new ownership entity, releases the seller from post-closing obligations, and aligns the County loan documents with the new senior financing structure;
An Allonge to Secured Promissory Note, which amends the original County Note to reflect the new borrower, modifies certain loan terms, and confirms the non-recourse nature of the County loan; and
A Subordination Agreement, which formally subordinates the County’s existing loan to the new senior bond financing, as required by the senior lender and Freddie Mac, while preserving the County’s regulatory and affordability enforcement rights
No changes are proposed to the affordability requirements established under the County’s existing Land Use Restriction Agreement. Affordability monitoring is conducted through the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program and the Housing Finance Authority’s bond compliance process.
This initiative aligns with strategic plan priorities TC 5.3.1: Promote and encourage a mix of housing types to address affordable, essential, and workforce housing needs and TC 5.3.5: Seek out and leverage state and federal funding sources to expand the housing inventory and improve housing affordability.

description:
The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) has issued its Fiscal Year 2025 formula allocation for the HOME Investment Partnerships (HOME) Program. As authorized by the Consolidated Appropriations Act (Public Law 119-4), St. Lucie County has been awarded $923,988.83 in HOME funds for FY 2025.
St. Lucie County serves as the Participating Jurisdiction and administrator for the HOME Consortium, which includes Indian River County, Martin County, the City of Port St. Lucie, the City of Fellsmere, and the Village of Indiantown. Individually, these jurisdictions would not meet the population threshold to receive HOME funds; however, collectively they qualify through the Consortium structure.
HUD transmitted the FY 2025 Federal Award Agreement for the HOME Program to the County for execution. The agreement establishes the terms and conditions governing the use of HOME funds, including compliance with federal statutes, HUD regulations at 24 C.F.R. Part 92, Uniform Administrative Requirements under 2 C.F.R. Part 200, environmental review requirements, and other applicable federal requirements .
HOME funds will be used to support eligible affordable housing activities consistent with the County’s HUD-approved Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan, including the development and rehabilitation of affordable housing for low-income and very low-income households. As required by federal regulation, a portion of the allocation may be reserved for administrative costs and Community Housing Development Organization (CHDO) activities.
This initiative aligns with Strategic Plan priority TC 5.3.5: Seek out and leverage state and federal funding sources to expand the housing inventory and improve housing affordability.
